\subsection*{Instruction-Tuned Model Results}

Table~\ref{tab:instruct} summarizes depth classification under instruction tuning for three model families.
All results use within-model 5-fold CV on single-generator chains; LOGO evaluation is available for two models but uses earlier generator subsets (5--6 generators), so cross-model numbers are not directly comparable across rows.

\begin{table}[ht]
\centering
\small
\caption{Depth classification: base vs.\ instruction-tuned models (within-model 5-fold CV). $\rho$: Spearman correlation of entropy mean with depth. Rev.: number of features (out of 7) whose $\rho$ reverses sign under instruction tuning.}
\label{tab:instruct}
\resizebox{\linewidth}{!}{%
\begin{tabular}{lcc cc cc c}
\toprule
& \multicolumn{2}{c}{\textbf{3-class F1}} & \multicolumn{2}{c}{\textbf{Binary F1}} & \multicolumn{2}{c}{$\boldsymbol{\rho}$\textbf{(ent.\ mean)}} & \\
\cmidrule(lr){2-3} \cmidrule(lr){4-5} \cmidrule(lr){6-7}
\textbf{Model} & Base & Instruct & Base & Instruct & Base & Instruct & \textbf{Rev.} \\
\midrule
OLMo-2-1B       & 0.754 & 0.575 & 0.845 & 0.813 & $-$0.64 & $+$0.48 & 6/7 \\
Qwen3-1.7B      & 0.769 & 0.732 & 0.861 & 0.875 & $-$0.60 & $+$0.48 & 6/7 \\
Llama-3.2-3B    & 0.742 & 0.544 & 0.849 & 0.838 & $-$0.63 & $+$0.23 & 3/7 \\
\bottomrule
\end{tabular}}
\end{table}

Instruction tuning degrades 3-class F1 by 3.7--19.9\,pp across all three families, while binary F1 (gen-1 vs.\ gen-2+) changes remain small ($|\Delta| \leq 3.2$\,pp).
The asymmetry indicates that instruction tuning primarily disrupts the gen-0/gen-1 boundary (human vs.\ first-generation), consistent with RLHF shifting the output distribution away from human-like text.
Entropy-mean $\rho$ reverses sign for all three models ($-0.60$--$-0.64$ base $\rightarrow$ $+0.23$--$+0.48$ instruct), and 6 of 7 features reverse for OLMo and Qwen vs.\ 3 of 7 for Llama.
This pattern is consistent with instruction tuning shifting the generation attractor rather than eliminating iterative dynamics (\S\ref{sec:discussion}).

\paragraph{Retraining on instruction-tuned data.}
To test whether the depth signal persists under instruction tuning with reversed polarity, we retrain the XGBoost classifier on instruction-tuned feature data (Table~\ref{tab:instruct-retrain}).

\begin{table}[ht]
\centering
\small
\caption{Classification recovery under instruction-tuned retraining (binary-only: gen-1 vs.\ gen-2+, gen-0 excluded from training and evaluation). Base$\rightarrow$Inst: base-trained classifier tested on instruct data. Note: Table~\ref{tab:instruct} reports higher instruct binary F1 (e.g., OLMo 0.813) because it uses 3-class training with binary evaluation, where gen-0 in training helps the classifier learn the feature space.}
\label{tab:instruct-retrain}
\begin{tabular}{lccc}
\toprule
\textbf{Model} & \textbf{Base$\rightarrow$Inst} & \textbf{Retrained} & \textbf{$\Delta$} \\
\midrule
OLMo-2-1B-Inst   & 0.321 & 0.590 & $+$0.269 \\
Qwen3-1.7B-Inst  & 0.500 & 0.660 & $+$0.160 \\
Qwen3-0.6B-Inst  & 0.532 & 0.600 & $+$0.068 \\
\bottomrule
\end{tabular}
\end{table}

Retraining recovers substantial within-model performance ($+$6.8--26.9\,pp), but the retrained F1 (0.590--0.660) remains below base-model levels (0.69--0.72).
Three-generator instruct LOGO yields binary F1\,=\,0.487, indicating weak cross-generator transfer under instruction tuning.

\paragraph{DDR structure under instruction tuning.}
$k{=}2$ clustering in $(|\rho|, d)$ space on pooled instruct features yields silhouette\,=\,0.338 (vs.\ 0.632 for base models), indicating that the clean drifting/non-drifting partition is substantially compressed.
The compression is model-dependent: OLMo-Instruct shows near-zero $|\rho|$ for TTR and hapax (0.006, 0.025), while Qwen instruct models retain moderate correlations ($|\rho|{=}0.48$--$0.53$).
Cross-condition transfer is near chance in both directions (base$\rightarrow$instruct binary F1\,=\,0.490; instruct$\rightarrow$base F1\,=\,0.454), with the asymmetry ($-$0.036) suggesting that instruct-trained features generalize even less to base distributions than the reverse.
These results indicate that instruction tuning compresses the feature-space structure underlying DDR rather than simply reversing feature directions.

\paragraph{End-to-end instruct classification.}
To test whether depth signal persists at the token level despite summary-statistic degradation, we apply the QLoRA end-to-end classifier (Appendix~\ref{app:qlora}) to instruction-tuned data using within-model 5-fold stratified CV (Table~\ref{tab:instruct-qlora}).

\begin{table}[ht]
\centering
\small
\caption{End-to-end QLoRA vs.\ XGBoost on instruction-tuned data (within-model 5-fold CV, Qwen3-0.6B backbone). Base QLoRA rows shown for reference only; instruct sets ($N{\approx}4.4$--$5.0$K) are approximately twice the base sets ($N{\approx}2.3$K), so cross-condition comparison is confounded by training set size.}
\label{tab:instruct-qlora}
\resizebox{\linewidth}{!}{%
\begin{tabular}{lccccc}
\toprule
& \multicolumn{2}{c}{\textbf{3-class F1}} & & \\
\cmidrule(lr){2-3}
\textbf{Model} & XGB & QLoRA & $\boldsymbol{\Delta}$ & \textbf{$N$} \\
\midrule
OLMo-2-1B-Inst   & 0.575 & 0.888\,$\pm$\,0.007 & $+$31.3\,pp & 4{,}429 \\
Qwen3-1.7B-Inst  & 0.732 & 0.907\,$\pm$\,0.008 & $+$17.5\,pp & 4{,}963 \\
\midrule
OLMo-2-1B (base) &       & 0.859\,$\pm$\,0.004 &             & 2{,}379 \\
Qwen3-1.7B (base)&       & 0.904\,$\pm$\,0.009 &             & 2{,}291 \\
\bottomrule
\end{tabular}}
\end{table}

The XGBoost-to-QLoRA gap on the same instruct data is substantial ($+$17.5 to $+$31.3\,pp), indicating that depth signal persists at the token level under instruction tuning but is inaccessible to the seven summary statistics; the degradation reported in Table~\ref{tab:instruct} reflects a feature-level limitation rather than signal absence.
Note that instruct samples are approximately twice the base count used here (Table~\ref{tab:instruct-qlora}), so the instruct-vs-base QLoRA comparison is confounded by training set size; the meaningful comparison is QLoRA-vs-XGBoost on the same instruct data.
All results use within-model 5-fold CV, not cross-generator LOGO, limiting generalization claims.

1	To assess whether depth signal extends beyond handcrafted features, we fine-tune a pretrained language model end-to-end as a depth classifier using QLoRA \cite{qlora}.
2	
3	\paragraph{Setup.}
4	We fine-tune Qwen3-0.6B-Base with LoRA rank 16, learning rate $2 \times 10^{-4}$, and 3 epochs, framing depth estimation as 5-class sequence classification (gen-0 through gen-4).\footnote{Evaluated on the original 6-generator subset; XGBoost 3-class F1\,=\,0.789. We expect 8-generator training to further improve given additional diversity; the comparison direction is preserved.}
5	For 3-class evaluation, we collapse predictions into gen-0\,/\,gen-1\,/\,gen-2+ post hoc.
6	All results use the same LOGO protocol as the main experiments.
7	
8	\begin{table}[ht]
9	\centering
10	\small
11	\caption{QLoRA end-to-end depth classification vs.\ XGBoost on handcrafted features, under LOGO evaluation.}
12	\label{tab:qlora}
13	\resizebox{\linewidth}{!}{%
14	\begin{tabular}{lccc}
15	\toprule
16	\textbf{Method} & \textbf{5-class F1} & \textbf{3-class F1} & \textbf{Per-class F1 (5-class)} \\
17	\midrule
18	XGBoost (7 features) & 0.501 $\pm$ 0.038 & 0.789 & --- \\
19	QLoRA (Qwen3-0.6B)   & 0.583 $\pm$ 0.010 & 0.905 $\pm$ 0.003 & 0.999\,/\,0.796\,/\,0.413\,/\,0.259\,/\,0.447 \\
20	\bottomrule
21	\end{tabular}}
22	\end{table}
23	
24	\paragraph{Results.}
25	QLoRA achieves 3-class LOGO F1\,=\,0.905 ($\pm$0.003), a +11.6\,pp improvement over the XGBoost baseline (0.789).
26	On 5-class evaluation, QLoRA reaches F1\,=\,0.583 ($\pm$0.010) vs.\ 0.501 for XGBoost (+8.2\,pp), with the largest gains at gen-1 (0.796 vs.\ 0.634) and gen-2 (0.413 vs.\ 0.268).
27	The gen-2/gen-3 boundary remains the primary failure mode (gen-3 F1\,=\,0.259), consistent with the feature-level analysis in \S\ref{sec:discussion}.
28	
29	\paragraph{Hyperparameter robustness.}
30	A second run with LoRA rank 32 and seed 123 yields 5-class F1\,=\,0.587 ($\pm$0.005) and 3-class F1\,=\,0.905 ($\pm$0.004), which confirms stability across hyperparameter and seed variation ($\Delta < 1$\,pp on both metrics).
31	
32	\paragraph{Implications.}
33	The substantial 3-class improvement demonstrates that raw token embeddings contain depth signal beyond what summary statistics capture; the seven handcrafted features are a strong but lossy compression of the full distributional information.
34	End-to-end fine-tuning exploits token-level patterns (e.g., positional regularities, n-gram repetitions) that aggregate features cannot represent.
35	This confirms that the depth signal documented in our main analysis is real and exploitable beyond engineered features, while the handcrafted approach retains practical advantages: interpretability, computational efficiency (no GPU inference), and the ability to reveal the differential depth response pattern that motivates the task formulation.
36

1	Can depth-aware data curation improve downstream language model quality?
2	We fine-tune OLMo-2-0425-1B on five data variants (3 seeds each) and evaluate perplexity on a held-out test set (Table~\ref{tab:downstream}).
3	
4	\begin{table}[ht]
5	\centering
6	\small
7	\begin{tabular}{lrc}
8	\toprule
9	\textbf{Variant} & \textbf{$n$} & \textbf{Test PPL} \\
10	\midrule
11	All depths            & 12{,}299 & 2.335 $\pm$ 0.000 \\
12	Size-matched (random) & 3{,}951  & 2.367 $\pm$ 0.000 \\
13	Depth 0--1 only       & 3{,}951  & 2.387 $\pm$ 0.001 \\
14	Binary-filtered       & 3{,}951  & 2.389 $\pm$ 0.000 \\
15	Depth 0 only          & 797      & 2.681 $\pm$ 0.001 \\
16	\bottomrule
17	\end{tabular}
18	\caption{Downstream fine-tuning perplexity (OLMo-2-0425-1B, mean $\pm$ std across 3 seeds). At equal sample count, random subsampling (2.367) outperforms depth-aware curation (depth 0--1: 2.387, binary-filtered: 2.389).}
19	\label{tab:downstream}
20	\end{table}
21	
22	The results are unambiguous: data quantity dominates depth composition.
23	Training on all 12{,}299 samples yields the lowest perplexity (2.335).
24	At equal sample count ($n$\,=\,3{,}951), random subsampling (2.367) \emph{outperforms} both depth-stratified selection (depth 0--1: 2.387) and binary detection filtering (2.389).
25	Cross-seed variance is below 0.002 across all variants, which confirms the robustness of this null result.
26	
27	Restricting training to human-only text (depth 0, $n$\,=\,797) produces a sharp perplexity increase to 2.681, driven primarily by the 5$\times$ reduction in data volume rather than depth composition per se.
28	
29	\paragraph{Equivalence testing.}
30	We apply a two one-sided $t$-test (TOST) with a $\pm$2\% relative margin (equivalence bounds $\pm$0.047 on the ppl scale) to formally assess whether the depth-aware and random subsampling conditions produce practically indistinguishable perplexity.
31	At equal sample count ($n$\,=\,3{,}951): size-matched (random) ppl\,=\,2.367 vs.\ depth 0--1 ppl\,=\,2.387, $\Delta$\,=\,0.020.
32	TOST confirms equivalence ($p = 1.1 \times 10^{-4}$); the two curation strategies yield practically indistinguishable downstream quality within the $\pm$2\% margin.
33	Cross-seed standard deviation is below 0.001 for both variants.
34	
35	Comparing the full dataset ($n$\,=\,12{,}299, ppl\,=\,2.335) against the depth-filtered subset ($n$\,=\,3{,}951, ppl\,=\,2.387): TOST \emph{rejects} equivalence (minimum equivalence margin\,=\,0.053, exceeding the $\pm$2\% bound), which confirms that data quantity drives perplexity reduction beyond what depth-aware selection can recover.
36	
37	Knowing the generation depth of a document does not, by itself, make it more or less useful for training; at fixed sample count, depth-aware curation is statistically equivalent to uninformed random subsampling.
38	
39	\subsection*{Margin Sensitivity Analysis}
40	
41	To assess the robustness of the equivalence conclusion to margin choice, we repeat the TOST procedure across multiple equivalence margins \cite{lakens_equivalence}, following the recommendation to report sensitivity across plausible bounds rather than relying on a single threshold (Table~\ref{tab:tost-margins}).
42	
43	\begin{table}[ht]
44	\centering
45	\small
46	\resizebox{\linewidth}{!}{%
47	\begin{tabular}{llcc}
48	\toprule
49	\textbf{Comparison} & \textbf{Margin} & \textbf{Equiv?} & \textbf{TOST $p$} \\
50	\midrule
51	Full (12{,}299) vs.\ Random (3{,}951) & $\pm$1\% & No & 1.0 \\
52	                                        & $\pm$2\% & Yes & $1 \times 10^{-6}$ \\
53	                                        & $\pm$3\% & Yes & $< 10^{-10}$ \\
54	                                        & $\pm$5\% & Yes & $< 10^{-10}$ \\
55	\midrule
56	Full (12{,}299) vs.\ Depth 0--1 (3{,}951) & $\pm$1\% & No & 1.0 \\
57	                                            & $\pm$2\% & No & 1.0 \\
58	                                            & $\pm$3\% & Yes & $< 10^{-10}$ \\
59	                                            & $\pm$5\% & Yes & $< 10^{-10}$ \\
60	\bottomrule
61	\end{tabular}}
62	\caption{TOST equivalence testing across multiple margins. ``Equiv?'' indicates whether equivalence is established at $\alpha = 0.05$.}
63	\label{tab:tost-margins}
64	\end{table}
65	
66	The full dataset vs.\ random subsample comparison passes equivalence at the $\pm$2\% margin ($p = 10^{-6}$), while the full vs.\ depth 0--1 comparison requires a $\pm$3\% margin.
67	In absolute terms, perplexity differences are small: $\Delta$\,=\,0.032 (full vs.\ random, 1.4\% of baseline) and $\Delta$\,=\,0.052 (full vs.\ depth 0--1, 2.2\% of baseline).
68	
69	Cohen's $d$ values are 86.0 (full vs.\ random) and 119.7 (full vs.\ depth 0--1).
70	These appear large but are unreliable: with only $n$\,=\,3 seeds per condition, the pooled standard deviation is extremely small ($<$0.001), artificially inflating $d$.
71	The inflated effect sizes reflect low seed-level variance (confirming reproducibility) rather than practically meaningful perplexity differences.
72	The TOST framework with pre-specified relative margins provides a more appropriate assessment than Cohen's $d$ in this low-seed regime.
73	However, with only $n{=}3$ seeds per condition, the TOST results have limited generalizability: the test is valid given observed variance but the conclusion generalizes over only three random seeds. We characterize this as a preliminary observation rather than a definitive null result.
74

Can depth-aware data curation improve downstream language model quality?
We fine-tune OLMo-2-0425-1B on five data variants (3 seeds each) and evaluate perplexity on a held-out test set (Table~\ref{tab:downstream}).

\begin{table}[ht]
\centering
\small
\begin{tabular}{lrc}
\toprule
\textbf{Variant} & \textbf{$n$} & \textbf{Test PPL} \\
\midrule
All depths            & 12{,}299 & 2.335 $\pm$ 0.000 \\
Size-matched (random) & 3{,}951  & 2.367 $\pm$ 0.000 \\
Depth 0--1 only       & 3{,}951  & 2.387 $\pm$ 0.001 \\
Binary-filtered       & 3{,}951  & 2.389 $\pm$ 0.000 \\
Depth 0 only          & 797      & 2.681 $\pm$ 0.001 \\
\bottomrule
\end{tabular}
\caption{Downstream fine-tuning perplexity (OLMo-2-0425-1B, mean $\pm$ std across 3 seeds). At equal sample count, random subsampling (2.367) outperforms depth-aware curation (depth 0--1: 2.387, binary-filtered: 2.389).}
\label{tab:downstream}
\end{table}

The results are unambiguous: data quantity dominates depth composition.
Training on all 12{,}299 samples yields the lowest perplexity (2.335).
At equal sample count ($n$\,=\,3{,}951), random subsampling (2.367) \emph{outperforms} both depth-stratified selection (depth 0--1: 2.387) and binary detection filtering (2.389).
Cross-seed variance is below 0.002 across all variants, which confirms the robustness of this null result.

Restricting training to human-only text (depth 0, $n$\,=\,797) produces a sharp perplexity increase to 2.681, driven primarily by the 5$\times$ reduction in data volume rather than depth composition per se.

\paragraph{Equivalence testing.}
We apply a two one-sided $t$-test (TOST) with a $\pm$2\% relative margin (equivalence bounds $\pm$0.047 on the ppl scale) to formally assess whether the depth-aware and random subsampling conditions produce practically indistinguishable perplexity.
At equal sample count ($n$\,=\,3{,}951): size-matched (random) ppl\,=\,2.367 vs.\ depth 0--1 ppl\,=\,2.387, $\Delta$\,=\,0.020.
TOST confirms equivalence ($p = 1.1 \times 10^{-4}$); the two curation strategies yield practically indistinguishable downstream quality within the $\pm$2\% margin.
Cross-seed standard deviation is below 0.001 for both variants.

Comparing the full dataset ($n$\,=\,12{,}299, ppl\,=\,2.335) against the depth-filtered subset ($n$\,=\,3{,}951, ppl\,=\,2.387): TOST \emph{rejects} equivalence (minimum equivalence margin\,=\,0.053, exceeding the $\pm$2\% bound), which confirms that data quantity drives perplexity reduction beyond what depth-aware selection can recover.

Knowing the generation depth of a document does not, by itself, make it more or less useful for training; at fixed sample count, depth-aware curation is statistically equivalent to uninformed random subsampling.

\subsection*{Margin Sensitivity Analysis}

To assess the robustness of the equivalence conclusion to margin choice, we repeat the TOST procedure across multiple equivalence margins \cite{lakens_equivalence}, following the recommendation to report sensitivity across plausible bounds rather than relying on a single threshold (Table~\ref{tab:tost-margins}).

\begin{table}[ht]
\centering
\small
\resizebox{\linewidth}{!}{%
\begin{tabular}{llcc}
\toprule
\textbf{Comparison} & \textbf{Margin} & \textbf{Equiv?} & \textbf{TOST $p$} \\
\midrule
Full (12{,}299) vs.\ Random (3{,}951) & $\pm$1\% & No & 1.0 \\
                                        & $\pm$2\% & Yes & $1 \times 10^{-6}$ \\
                                        & $\pm$3\% & Yes & $< 10^{-10}$ \\
                                        & $\pm$5\% & Yes & $< 10^{-10}$ \\
\midrule
Full (12{,}299) vs.\ Depth 0--1 (3{,}951) & $\pm$1\% & No & 1.0 \\
                                            & $\pm$2\% & No & 1.0 \\
                                            & $\pm$3\% & Yes & $< 10^{-10}$ \\
                                            & $\pm$5\% & Yes & $< 10^{-10}$ \\
\bottomrule
\end{tabular}}
\caption{TOST equivalence testing across multiple margins. ``Equiv?'' indicates whether equivalence is established at $\alpha = 0.05$.}
\label{tab:tost-margins}
\end{table}

The full dataset vs.\ random subsample comparison passes equivalence at the $\pm$2\% margin ($p = 10^{-6}$), while the full vs.\ depth 0--1 comparison requires a $\pm$3\% margin.
In absolute terms, perplexity differences are small: $\Delta$\,=\,0.032 (full vs.\ random, 1.4\% of baseline) and $\Delta$\,=\,0.052 (full vs.\ depth 0--1, 2.2\% of baseline).

Cohen's $d$ values are 86.0 (full vs.\ random) and 119.7 (full vs.\ depth 0--1).
These appear large but are unreliable: with only $n$\,=\,3 seeds per condition, the pooled standard deviation is extremely small ($<$0.001), artificially inflating $d$.
The inflated effect sizes reflect low seed-level variance (confirming reproducibility) rather than practically meaningful perplexity differences.
The TOST framework with pre-specified relative margins provides a more appropriate assessment than Cohen's $d$ in this low-seed regime.
However, with only $n{=}3$ seeds per condition, the TOST results have limited generalizability: the test is valid given observed variance but the conclusion generalizes over only three random seeds. We characterize this as a preliminary observation rather than a definitive null result.

\section*{Limitations}
\label{sec:limitations}

All eight generators are base (pretrained) models.
This is a deliberate design choice: base models isolate the generation mechanism from instruction-tuning effects, enabling controlled study of recursive distributional drift.
However, web text is predominantly produced by instruction-tuned and RLHF-aligned models.
Preliminary instruct experiments confirm that depth signal degrades substantially under instruction tuning: OLMo-2-1B-Instruct drops to LOGO F1\,=\,0.338 (vs.\ 0.763 base) and Qwen3-0.6B with chat template to 0.667 (vs.\ 0.816 under a 7-generator split).
Length-matched analysis yields near-zero correlations ($|\rho| < 0.02$) and binary classification near chance (F1\,$\approx$\,0.5) for Qwen models, leaving interpretation ambiguous.
Extending depth fingerprinting to instruct models requires addressing these confounds (length regulation, format constraints, safety-driven distribution shaping) that instruction tuning introduces.

Our experiments include generators up to 8.2B parameters (Qwen3-8B).
Depth signal persists at this scale (Qwen3-8B 3-class F1\,=\,0.714), but cross-scale transfer incurs a moderate gap vs.\ $\leq$2.8B generators (F1\,=\,0.77--0.81).
Gemma-2-2B shows the weakest generalization among nine generators (3-class F1\,=\,0.628), with gen-1 nearly indistinguishable from other classes (per-class F1\,=\,0.036); this architecture-specific limitation is discussed in Appendix~\ref{app:9gen-scale}.
Frontier models (70B+) remain untested; their higher fluency may further compress feature margins.

Differential depth response strength is prompt-type dependent: within-type 3-class F1 ranges from 0.78 (continuation) to 0.73 (elaboration), with inspired rewriting intermediate at 0.74 (Appendix~\ref{app:prompt-type}).
DDR is most reliably detected in continuation-style generation; near-paraphrastic settings approach the method's detection floor.
Cross-prompt-type transfer (LOPTO F1\,=\,0.753) confirms shared signal, yet additional prompt types (e.g., summarization, instruction following) and cross-generator $\times$ cross-prompt interactions remain untested.

Our primary evaluation uses single-generator chains; cross-model chains (\S\ref{sec:results-classification}) confirm depth signal under generator heterogeneity (3-class F1\,=\,0.789, binary F1\,=\,0.830; evaluated on the 5-generator subset for which cross-model chains were available), though these generators represent a controlled laboratory setting rather than the full diversity of real-world contamination.
Simulated human editing (\S\ref{sec:discussion}) suggests graceful degradation, but the gap between simulated token replacement and real-world post-processing remains untested.
Independent gen-0 seed sets per generator would eliminate potential memorization effects in 3-class LOGO evaluation; we report leak-free binary F1 as the primary metric to mitigate this limitation.

The reference model is fixed to Pythia-410M throughout, although cross-family reference experiments (\S\ref{sec:results-differential}) confirm the phenomenon is not reference-specific (spread 0.013 across three references).
All seed texts in the main evaluation are English Wikipedia excerpts.
Cross-domain evaluation (Appendix~\ref{app:domain}) shows that depth signal persists across News, Academic, and Code domains (binary F1 $>$ 0.73 under LOGO at $t{=}1.0$), though a domain $\times$ temperature interaction exists: certain domain/generator combinations at lower temperature approach chance level (e.g., Academic domain binary F1\,=\,0.628 at $t{=}0.7$), suggesting that reference model calibration is critical for cross-domain deployment.
The reference model dependency (Pythia-410M, English-centric pretraining) limits non-English applicability and adds inference overhead relative to surface-feature-only approaches.
Generalization to other languages remains untested.

Our default analysis uses fixed decoding parameters (temperature 0.7, nucleus $p{=}0.9$). A sampling ablation (Appendix~\ref{app:sampling-sensitivity}) shows robustness to moderate variation ($t \in [0.5, 0.7]$, ${\leq}0.3$\,pp) but substantial degradation at $t{=}1.0$ ($-6$\,pp), indicating that depth fingerprinting assumes standard decoding regimes.
Cross-temperature transfer shows substantial degradation when test-time temperature exceeds training-time settings, limiting deployment to scenarios where the generation temperature is approximately known.

We use 3-class granularity (gen-0\,/\,gen-1\,/\,gen-2+). A 5-class evaluation (Appendix~\ref{app:finer-depth}) yields LOGO F1\,$\approx$\,0.50, with depths 2--4 mutually indistinguishable, validating the 3-class design as the practical resolution limit.

1	\section{Discussion}
2	\label{sec:discussion}
3	
4	Recursive generation alters \emph{where} the token-level surprise distribution sits but not \emph{how} it is shaped.
5	A plausible mechanism is mode-seeking behavior in nucleus sampling: top-$p$ truncation selects from a fixed probability-mass fraction, preserving the shape of the conditional distribution (tail decay, entropy extremes), while the \emph{input} to this truncation shifts as the model conditions on its own increasingly typical outputs, compressing mean surprisal.
6	Each recursive step feeds a slightly more ``self-typical'' input into the same truncation mechanism, producing monotonic location drift at stable shape.
7	This account predicts that increasing randomness should weaken the drift, and the data confirm it: at $t{=}1.0$, location signal collapses ($\rho$ from $-0.60$ to $-0.002$; Appendix~\ref{app:sampling-sensitivity}), consistent with higher temperature diluting the mode-seeking tendency.
8	Semantic-preservation constraints similarly attenuate drift (elaboration F1\,=\,0.730 vs.\ continuation 0.781; Appendix~\ref{app:prompt-type}), consistent with \citet{broken_telephone}; cross-type transfer remains viable (F1\,=\,0.753).
9	Permutation importance, Granger causality, and feature intervention analyses confirm that DDR captures causal predictive structure: drifting features contribute $5.5\times$ more to classification than near-stationary ones, and 6/7 features exhibit significant Granger causality, with entropy\_min as the sole exception (Appendix~\ref{app:ddr-causality}).
10	
11	Several boundary conditions constrain practical applicability.
12	Document-level gen-1 per-class F1\,=\,0.63 is insufficient for automated filtering but sufficient for corpus-level flagging ($O(1/\sqrt{n})$ error scaling); the primary difficulty is distinguishing gen-1 from gen-2+, consistent with DDR producing the smallest location shift at the first recursive step (86\% false negatives; Appendix~\ref{app:error-analysis}).
13	Two diagnostic scenarios illustrate practical utility: (a)~training-data batch auditing, where batches exceeding a gen-2+ proportion threshold trigger review; (b)~provenance tracing, where known gen-0 seeds enable lineage reconstruction through successive depth predictions.
14	In generator-unknown deployment, the 9.1\,pp per-generator spread represents estimation uncertainty; the ensemble LOGO F1\,=\,0.694 provides a conservative lower bound, stable across reference model families (F1 within 0.013; Table~\ref{tab:cross-ref}).
15	Cross-temperature transfer degrades when test-time temperature exceeds training (F1 drops to 0.723; worst-case per-generator F1\,=\,0.418; Appendix~\ref{app:cross-temp}).
16	
17	Preliminary evidence from a 14.7B generator (Qwen3-14B-Base) confirms that the DDR partition persists at larger scale: Cohen's $d$ for drifting features remains in the large-effect range ($d{=}0.78$--$1.12$), though Spearman $|\rho|$ attenuates by 21--35\%, with entropy mean approaching the drifting boundary ($|\rho|{=}0.39$, $d{=}0.78$).
18	This scale-dependent signal compression is consistent with larger models producing more self-typical outputs that narrow inter-depth contrasts; the partition structure is preserved even as absolute effect sizes compress.
19	
20	DDR connects to but differs from model collapse \cite{curse_of_recursion,strong_model_collapse}.
21	Both phenomena reflect distributional compression under iterative processing: DDR's drifting features (entropy mean, TTR, hapax ratio) capture the same lexical diversity loss documented as ``diversity collapse'' in retraining studies, where minority modes progressively vanish \cite{strong_model_collapse}.
22	The key difference is mechanism and reversibility: retraining permanently erodes tail coverage by updating parameters, while inference-chain drift at fixed parameters shifts only location, leaving shape features as stable references.
23	This distinction is what makes depth detection viable: near-stationary features provide an invariant baseline against which location drift becomes measurable.
24	Three depth classes represent the practical resolution ceiling (5-class F1\,$\approx$\,0.50; Appendix~\ref{app:finer-depth}), though richer representations recover substantially more signal (QLoRA F1\,=\,0.905; Appendix~\ref{app:qlora}).
25	Instruction-tuned models show attenuated fingerprints (OLMo-Instruct LOGO F1\,=\,0.338 vs.\ 0.763 base) with reversed feature correlations, suggesting alignment reshapes the generation attractor rather than eliminating depth signal; QLoRA recovers to F1\,=\,0.89--0.91 on instruct data (Appendix~\ref{app:instruct}), confirming token-level signal persists despite summary-statistic degradation.
26

\section{Discussion}
\label{sec:discussion}

Recursive generation alters \emph{where} the token-level surprise distribution sits but not \emph{how} it is shaped.
A plausible mechanism is mode-seeking behavior in nucleus sampling: top-$p$ truncation selects from a fixed probability-mass fraction, preserving the shape of the conditional distribution (tail decay, entropy extremes), while the \emph{input} to this truncation shifts as the model conditions on its own increasingly typical outputs, compressing mean surprisal.
Each recursive step feeds a slightly more ``self-typical'' input into the same truncation mechanism, producing monotonic location drift at stable shape.
This account predicts that increasing randomness should weaken the drift, and the data confirm it: at $t{=}1.0$, location signal collapses ($\rho$ from $-0.60$ to $-0.002$; Appendix~\ref{app:sampling-sensitivity}), consistent with higher temperature diluting the mode-seeking tendency.
Semantic-preservation constraints similarly attenuate drift (elaboration F1\,=\,0.730 vs.\ continuation 0.781; Appendix~\ref{app:prompt-type}), consistent with \citet{broken_telephone}; cross-type transfer remains viable (F1\,=\,0.753).
Permutation importance, Granger causality, and feature intervention analyses confirm that DDR captures causal predictive structure: drifting features contribute $5.5\times$ more to classification than near-stationary ones, and 6/7 features exhibit significant Granger causality, with entropy\_min as the sole exception (Appendix~\ref{app:ddr-causality}).

Several boundary conditions constrain practical applicability.
Document-level gen-1 per-class F1\,=\,0.63 is insufficient for automated filtering but sufficient for corpus-level flagging ($O(1/\sqrt{n})$ error scaling); the primary difficulty is distinguishing gen-1 from gen-2+, consistent with DDR producing the smallest location shift at the first recursive step (86\% false negatives; Appendix~\ref{app:error-analysis}).
Two diagnostic scenarios illustrate practical utility: (a)~training-data batch auditing, where batches exceeding a gen-2+ proportion threshold trigger review; (b)~provenance tracing, where known gen-0 seeds enable lineage reconstruction through successive depth predictions.
In generator-unknown deployment, the 9.1\,pp per-generator spread represents estimation uncertainty; the ensemble LOGO F1\,=\,0.694 provides a conservative lower bound, stable across reference model families (F1 within 0.013; Table~\ref{tab:cross-ref}).
Cross-temperature transfer degrades when test-time temperature exceeds training (F1 drops to 0.723; worst-case per-generator F1\,=\,0.418; Appendix~\ref{app:cross-temp}).

Preliminary evidence from a 14.7B generator (Qwen3-14B-Base) confirms that the DDR partition persists at larger scale: Cohen's $d$ for drifting features remains in the large-effect range ($d{=}0.78$--$1.12$), though Spearman $|\rho|$ attenuates by 21--35\%, with entropy mean approaching the drifting boundary ($|\rho|{=}0.39$, $d{=}0.78$).
This scale-dependent signal compression is consistent with larger models producing more self-typical outputs that narrow inter-depth contrasts; the partition structure is preserved even as absolute effect sizes compress.

DDR connects to but differs from model collapse \cite{curse_of_recursion,strong_model_collapse}.
Both phenomena reflect distributional compression under iterative processing: DDR's drifting features (entropy mean, TTR, hapax ratio) capture the same lexical diversity loss documented as ``diversity collapse'' in retraining studies, where minority modes progressively vanish \cite{strong_model_collapse}.
The key difference is mechanism and reversibility: retraining permanently erodes tail coverage by updating parameters, while inference-chain drift at fixed parameters shifts only location, leaving shape features as stable references.
This distinction is what makes depth detection viable: near-stationary features provide an invariant baseline against which location drift becomes measurable.
Three depth classes represent the practical resolution ceiling (5-class F1\,$\approx$\,0.50; Appendix~\ref{app:finer-depth}), though richer representations recover substantially more signal (QLoRA F1\,=\,0.905; Appendix~\ref{app:qlora}).
Instruction-tuned models show attenuated fingerprints (OLMo-Instruct LOGO F1\,=\,0.338 vs.\ 0.763 base) with reversed feature correlations, suggesting alignment reshapes the generation attractor rather than eliminating depth signal; QLoRA recovers to F1\,=\,0.89--0.91 on instruct data (Appendix~\ref{app:instruct}), confirming token-level signal persists despite summary-statistic degradation.

% Abstract — Depth Fingerprinting of Recursive LLM Generation Chains
\begin{abstract}
Recursive generation by base (pretrained) LLMs shifts \emph{where} text sits in distributional space but leaves \emph{how} it is shaped nearly unchanged, and this asymmetry is consistent across five model families spanning 0.6B to 8B parameters.
We term this \emph{differential depth response} (DDR): under standard decoding (temperature $\leq 0.7$, nucleus $p{=}0.9$), mean entropy and lexical diversity drift monotonically with generation depth while entropy max and tail decay show an order-of-magnitude smaller effect size.
Prior work on iterative generation tracks aggregate convergence without separating what changes from what is preserved; DDR provides this decomposition and enables coarse depth classification (gen-0\,/\,gen-1\,/\,gen-2+): a 7-feature ensemble achieves leak-free binary F1\,=\,0.694 (95\% CI [.688, .700]) under leave-one-generator-out evaluation and 0.830 on cross-model chains (5-generator subset, LOGO; 95\% CI [.818, .841]), at lower cost than multi-detector alternatives.
Despite measurable distributional drift, preliminary equivalence testing (TOST $\pm$2\%, $p < 0.001$; $n{=}3$ seeds) suggests no downstream training quality degradation.
The depth signal degrades under instruction tuning; current applicability is restricted to base models.
\end{abstract}

\section{Introduction}
\label{sec:introduction}

Existing AI text detection addresses a single question: is this text human or machine \cite{detectgpt,fast_detectgpt,binoculars,ld_score}?
This binary framing is a blind spot.
As LLM outputs re-enter training corpora \cite{dolma,fineweb} and seed further generation, web text accumulates at varying recursive depths: an estimated 7--17\% of recent scientific publications contain substantial LLM-modified content \cite{mapping_llm_science,monitoring_ai_review}, each generation cycle producing text qualitatively different from both its human source and its first-generation predecessor.
Distinguishing these depths matters for data provenance \cite{ccnet,dsir} and model collapse theory \cite{curse_of_recursion,strong_model_collapse}, but no current method addresses it.

We introduce \emph{depth fingerprinting}: classifying text by ordinal generation depth (gen-0\,/\,gen-1\,/\,gen-2+) and decomposing the distributional drift across depths into structurally distinct components.
The core finding is a \emph{differential depth response} (DDR): across eight base-model generators from five families (0.6B--8B), the NLL distribution's central tendency (mean entropy, lexical diversity) drifts monotonically with depth while its shape (entropy extremes, tail structure) remains an order of magnitude more stable ($d{=}0.76$--$1.17$ vs.\ $d < 0.10$).
This location/shape asymmetry has analytical value independent of classification: it reveals that fixed-parameter autoregressive sampling systematically compresses distributional location while preserving higher-order structure, a pattern distinct from the tail-coverage erosion in model collapse \cite{curse_of_recursion}.
Concurrent studies characterize convergence in paraphrastic and translation chains \cite{broken_telephone,markovian_chains}; ours is the first to decompose the drift mechanism and exploit the asymmetry for cross-generator depth prediction.
We restrict to base (pretrained) models to isolate generation dynamics from alignment artifacts (\S\ref{sec:discussion}).

The DDR decomposition enables practical depth classification: binary F1\,=\,0.694 under leave-one-generator-out evaluation, 0.830 on heterogeneous cross-model chains, outperforming individual detection baselines by 6.7--36.3\,pp at 2.4$\times$ lower inference cost than multi-detector ensembles.

Our contributions:
\begin{enumerate}[nosep,leftmargin=*]
    \item \textbf{Analytical finding.} Inference-chain drift decomposes into a location component ($d{=}0.76$--$1.17$) and a stable shape component ($d < 0.10$), a separation absent from existing detection, model collapse, and attractor dynamics analyses and with diagnostic value beyond classification.
    \item \textbf{Task and evaluation suite.} We formulate generation depth classification and construct a dataset of 37K texts from eight generators spanning five model families (0.6B--8B), evaluated under leave-one-generator-out cross-validation.
    \item \textbf{Practical depth classifier.} A 7-feature ensemble exploiting DDR achieves binary F1\,=\,0.830 on cross-model chains, with systematic boundary analysis across temperature, prompt type, instruction tuning, and downstream quality.
\end{enumerate}

   - The paper acknowledges this discrepancy (results.tex line 89) but frames it as "distributional shape change without location shift"
   - This is a principled finding, but the near-stationary label is misleading — entropy_min is near-stationary in location only, not in rank-order distribution
   - **Impact**: The "3/1/3 partition" would more honestly be described as "3/1/2+1_boundary" — the clean partition narrative breaks down

2. **TOST statistical power is severely limited for the DDR partition claim**
   - Looking at the per-generator TOST results, tail_decay passes for only 4 out of 8 generators at ε=0.20, and entropy_max passes for 6 out of 8. The generators that fail tail_decay have effect sizes between 0.15-0.22, which are borderline rather than clearly negligible. The bootstrap TOST approach pools all data (N=29,095) and achieves 100% rejection, but that's expected with such enormous statistical power — the per-generator analysis is more revealing and shows the partition doesn't hold robustly for tail_decay. The claim in results.tex line 91 that "the partition is not a pooling artifact" overstates the case; tail_decay specifically shows borderline behavior.

3. **The 3

/1/3 partition is post-hoc data-driven, not principled**
   - k-means clustering at k=2 produces a clean silhouette score of 0.632 and naturally separates drifting from non-drifting generators. At k=3, the silhouette drops to 0.499 and entropy_min forms its own cluster, but the paper's actual 3/1/3 partition doesn't match this clustering solution — entropy_std ends up intermediate and entropy_min near-stationary, which requires "domain-informed refinement" to override what the data suggests. The clean data-driven split is fundamentally 2-way; the 3/1/3 breakdown is a post-hoc narrative imposed afterward.
   - The paper should lead with the 2-way split as the primary finding and present the 3/1/3 as one possible refinement.

The downstream utility experiment shows a null result that's framed ambiguously. When sample counts are equal, random subsampling actually outperforms depth-aware curation (2.367 vs 2.387), which is the opposite of what you'd hope for. The paper frames this as "data quantity dominates depth composition," but that understates it — depth-aware filtering is actively worse than random. While TOST equivalence at ±2% is established and n=3 seeds is acknowledged as insufficient, the abstract claims "no downstream training quality degradation," which is technically true but also means the depth fingerprinting has no demonstrated downstream value.

QLoRA's +11.6 percentage point improvement over the 7-feature approach is a major problem. QLoRA achieves 0.905 F1 on the 3-class task while the 7-feature XGBoost only reaches 0.789, and on instruct data QLoRA recovers to 0.89-0.91 while the 7-feature approach collapses. The paper uses QLoRA as evidence that "depth signal is real," but it simultaneously shows that the 7-feature approach captures only a fraction of the available signal — if the contribution is meant to be a practical depth classifier, this makes it look insufficient.

The base-model-only limitation is acknowledged in the abstract now, which is good, but the title doesn't reflect this constraint prominently enough.  The instruct LOGO results show F1=0.487 on 3 generators, which is near chance for a 3-class problem, meaning the method essentially fails on instruct models.

Cross-model chain evaluation has a confounding issue that the paper acknowledges. The single-generator transfer analysis (F1=0.810) is offered as counter-evidence, but it's a different setup entirely — training on one model and testing on another with all single-generator chains. When depth 1 uses generator A and depth 2 uses generator B in cross-model chains, the distributional shift compounds with model heterogeneity, creating a stronger signal that conflates depth with generator identity.

The baseline comparison is structurally unfair because the 7-feature approach is compared against single-score baselines with just one feature each. While the paper uses the same XGBoost framework, the 4-detector ensemble with 6 features actually outperforms the 7-feature approach (binary F1=0.708 vs 0.705), which undermines the practical contribution claim. A fairer comparison would pit the 7-feature method directly against the 4-detector ensemble, where it actually loses.

There's also an inconsistency with Bonferroni correction — the method section states all p-values use Bonferroni correction within each test family, but the TOST tests in the appendix apply individual α=0.05 per generator without correcting for multiple generators.

The LOFO analysis uses a 6-generator subset rather than the full 8-generator LOGO protocol used in the main results, making the baselines incomparable (F1=0.789 for 6-gen vs 0.762 for 8-gen). Figure 1 also dual-encodes both Spearman correlation and per-generator variation through strip plot width, which creates ambiguity in what's being visualized.

Now I'm moving into the formal review scoring. For soundness, the core DDR finding holds up well, but the 3/1/3 partition appears to be a post-hoc refinement rather than something discovered from the data itself—entropy minimization's classification contradicts this, and the TOST test for tail_decay is underpowered. The statistical methods are generally solid but make some overclaims. On excitement, the task is novel and the analytical finding is interesting, though the practical impact is moderate with F1=0.694 on base models, and QLoRA demonstrates the value of the handcrafted features.

For reproducibility, the paper excels with extensive implementation details, promised code and data, specified seeds and hyperparameters. Overall, I'm settling on 3.5/5—borderline for a top conference. The DDR decomposition is a genuine contribution and the evaluation is remarkably thorough, but the 3/1/3 partition feels like narrative overfitting, the practical gains are limited to base models, and there's no downstream utility demonstrated.

Actually, stepping back to reassess more carefully: the paper has substantial strengths—genuinely novel task formulation, a clean DDR finding at least for the 2-way split, exhaustive evaluation with 25+ appendix sections, honest acknowledgment of limitations, and sound statistical methodology overall. The negatives are worth weighing against these.

The weaknesses are real though: the 3/1/3 partition is post-hoc and doesn't align with k-means clustering, entropy minimization produces contradictory classifications, tail decay only passes statistical tests for 4 out of 8 generators, instruction-tuning fails, the F1 score of 0.694 is moderate at best, there's no downstream utility, and QLoRA undermines the practical value of the 7-feature approach. For EMNLP through ARR, 3.5 feels right—the DDR insight and evaluation rigor are genuinely strong, but the overclaimed 3/1/3 partition and practical limitations prevent a higher score.

## Reviewer 1 — Round 1 完整审稿报告（方法严谨性 + 实验设计）

**论文**: "Depth Fingerprinting: Detecting Recursive Generation Depth in LLM Text Chains"
**Venue**: EMNLP 2026 via ACL Rolling Review (Long Paper)

---

## Summary

本文提出 depth fingerprinting——将文本按递归生成深度分类为 gen-0/gen-1/gen-2+。核心分析发现 Differential Depth Response (DDR): 在 8 个 base model 生成器上，NLL 分布的位置特征（entropy mean、TTR、hapax ratio）随深度单调漂移（Cohen's d=0.76–1.17），而形状特征（entropy max、tail decay）保持近乎不变（d<0.10）。7-feature XGBoost ensemble 在 LOGO CV 下 binary F1=0.694，cross-model chains 上 0.830。QLoRA end-to-end 达 3-class F1=0.905。实验仅限 base model；instruct model 上显著退化。附录极为详尽（21 页，25+ 子节）。

---

## Strengths

**S1. 任务定义新颖且有意义。** 将 binary detection 扩展到 ordinal depth estimation 是一个自然但尚未被充分探索的方向。与 model collapse、数据溯源的联系增强了研究动机。

**S2. DDR 的二元分解（drifting vs. non-drifting）有扎实的实证支持。** k=2 clustering（silhouette=0.632）、5 种 effect-size 指标交叉验证、holdout generator split（Table 31, Δ|ρ| ≤ 0.05）、bootstrap TOST（100% rejection for near-stationary features）——证据链条在二元分解层面是收敛的。这是论文最有价值的发现。

**S3. 评估协议设计严谨。** LOGO CV 是跨生成器泛化的正确选择；binary F1（排除 gen-0）消除了 seed-sharing 泄漏；independent-seed control（F1=0.680 vs. 0.694）进一步确认信号来自生成退化而非主题。Bonferroni 校正和 bootstrap CI 的使用总体正确。

**S4. 自我批判程度罕见。** Abstract 明确说 "The depth signal degrades under instruction tuning; current applicability is restricted to base models"。Limitations section（page 9）诚实列举了温度敏感性、instruct 退化、scale 限制等。这种诚实度在投稿中不常见。

**S5. 附录的覆盖广度和深度令人印象深刻。** LOFO、TOST、bootstrap、Granger causality、permutation importance、cross-temp、cross-domain、instruct、downstream、error analysis、qualitative examples——几乎穷尽了所有合理的 robustness check。

---

## Weaknesses

### Critical

**C1. 3/1/3 partition 是 post-hoc 叙事构建，而非数据驱动发现**
- 具体位置：Section 4.2 (results.tex L65–80), Appendix DDR Validation (appendix_ddr_validation.tex)
- 论文声称 "Data-driven clustering confirms this as the dominant structure"（L65），但实际 k-means 结果 **不** 支持 3/1/3：
  - k=2（silhouette=0.632）: {drifting} | {non-drifting} — **这是数据支持的唯一 clean split**
  - k=3（silhouette=0.499, **更差**）: entropy_min 形成独立 cluster，而非 entropy_std
  - k=4（silhouette=0.571）: entropy_std 分离出来
- 论文的 3/1/3（entropy_std 为 intermediate, entropy_min 为 near-stationary）**不匹配任何 k-means 解**。获得 3/1/3 需要 "domain-informed refinement that unsupervised clustering cannot recover from pooled statistics alone"（appendix_ddr_validation.tex L24）——换言之，这是人为施加的分类，不是发现。
- **影响**：论文将 3/1/3 partition 作为核心贡献之一（Contribution 1: "a separation absent from existing detection"），但这个 partition 的 granularity 超出了数据支持的范围。数据支持的是 2-way split（drifting vs. non-drifting），不是 3/1/3。
- **建议**：将 2-way split 作为核心发现，3/1/3 作为 secondary refinement 并明确标注其 domain-informed 性质。在 Section 4.2 中将 k=2 silhouette=0.632 放在首位，而非用 3/1/3 来 frame 整个 DDR。

**C2. Entropy min 的分类存在根本性矛盾**
- 具体位置：results.tex L88–89, appendix_ddr_validation.tex L161–173
- Pooled |ρ|=0.40——这远离 near-stationary 区域（|ρ|<0.10），实际落在 intermediate 和 drifting 之间
- Cohen's d=0.016（near-stationary），但 Cliff's δ=0.354（"medium" effect）——两个指标给出矛盾结论
- k=3 clustering 将 entropy_min 分出独立 cluster，而非归入 near-stationary
- 论文的辩护（L89）："distributional shape change without location shift: recursive generation produces more extreme minimum-entropy tokens while preserving the mean"——这承认了 entropy_min 确实在变化，只是变化方式不同
- **影响**：将一个 |ρ|=0.40、Cliff's δ=0.354 的特征标记为 "near-stationary" 并与 |ρ|<0.10 的特征归为一组，在统计学上缺乏一致性。"Near-stationary" 标签专门针对 location stability 而非 rank-order stability——但论文的 partition 名称暗示了全面的稳定性。
- **建议**：至少将 entropy_min 标记为 "boundary feature"（如 entropy_std 被标为 intermediate），或更换 DDR partition 为 3/2/2（drifting / boundary / near-stationary），其中 entropy_std 和 entropy_min 都归入 boundary。

**C3. TOST 对 tail_decay 的近乎不变性检验不充分——partition 在该特征上实际是 borderline**
- 具体位置：appendix_tost.tex Table, appendix_ddr_validation.tex Table
- Per-generator TOST (ε=0.20): tail_decay 仅 4/8 generators pass equivalence（通过率 50%）
- 4 个未通过的 generator 的 |d| = 0.07–0.22（Llama 0.19, OLMo 0.22, Qwen-8B 0.15, Mistral 0.16）——OLMo 的 d=0.22 超过了 near-stationary 的 d=0.20 阈值
- 即使放宽到 ε=0.25，仍有 1/8 未通过（Llama-3.2-3B, d=0.19）
- Bootstrap TOST（appendix_tost_bootstrap.tex）在 pooled 数据（N=29,095）上 100% rejection——但这是因为样本量巨大导致 statistical power 极高，几乎任何小 effect 都会被 equivalence test 接受。这不能替代 per-generator 结论。
- 论文自己在 results.tex L94 承认："Tail decay shows generator-dependent variation (d=0.15–0.22), but reclassifying it as intermediate preserves the core split and classification performance."——这实际上承认 tail_decay 的 near-stationary 状态是可争议的。
- **影响**：3/1/3 partition 中，tail_decay 的 near-stationary 归类仅在一半的 generators 上通过检验。这削弱了 "the partition is robust at the individual-generator level"（appendix_tost.tex L12）的声明。
- **建议**：(1) 在主文中明确说明 tail_decay 的 borderline 状态；(2) 提出 3/1/2+1（drifting / intermediate / robust-near-stat / borderline-near-stat）作为更诚实的 partition；(3) 或至少将 TOST 4/8 的结果纳入 Section 4.2 而非仅放在附录。

### Major

**M1. TOST equivalence testing 的 power analysis 缺失**
- 具体位置：appendix_tost.tex, appendix_tost_bootstrap.tex
- Per-generator TOST 使用约 n≈3,500–4,500 samples per generator（37,058 / 8 generators / ~2 depth classes），在如此大样本下 TOST 几乎总能检测到 equivalence（如果真实 effect 不是零的话）
- 但论文从未报告 TOST 的 statistical power（给定 ε=0.20，在观察到的样本量和方差下，检测到 d=0.15 的非等价性的 power 是多少？）
- Downstream TOST（appendix_downstream.tex L70–72）中论文承认 n=3 seeds 时 Cohen's d 不可靠（d=86.0, "artificially inflating d"）——但对 DDR TOST 中大样本导致的反向问题（几乎任何小 effect 都通过 equivalence test）未做类似讨论
- **建议**：补充 power analysis，报告 per-generator TOST 在实际样本量和 ε=0.20 下能区分 d=0.10 vs d=0.20 的 power

**M2. Downstream utility 实际是 null result，但 framing 含糊**
- 具体位置：appendix_downstream.tex, abstract (abstract.tex L6)
- 核心发现：equal sample count 下，random subsampling (PPL=2.367) **优于** depth-aware curation (PPL=2.387, 2.389)——方向相反
- Abstract 说 "no downstream training quality degradation"——技术上正确（深层生成文本不比浅层差），但实际含义是 depth fingerprinting 对数据清洗 **无用**
- n=3 seeds（论文自己承认 "a preliminary observation rather than a definitive null result"）
- **影响**：Introduction L21 将 "downstream quality" 列为 boundary analysis 的一部分——但实验实际显示无正面效果。这应该更透明地呈现。
- **建议**：(1) Abstract 中改为 "depth composition does not affect downstream quality at tested scale"；(2) 删除或大幅缩减 downstream 作为 contribution 的权重

**M3. QLoRA 的 +11.6pp 反衬了 7-feature 方法的局限性**
- 具体位置：appendix_qlora.tex, results.tex L19–20
- QLoRA 3-class F1=0.905 vs 7-feature 0.789（gap=11.6pp）
- 在 instruct 数据上更明显：QLoRA 0.888–0.907 vs XGBoost 0.575–0.732
- 论文将此定位为 "confirms that DDR's primary contribution is the empirical decomposition, not the specific classifier"（L20）——这是诚实的
- 但问题是：如果 QLoRA 用 token-level features 远超 7 个 handcrafted features，那 7 个特征是否真的 "capture" 了 DDR？还是仅捕获了 DDR 的一个粗糙近似？
- **影响**：削弱了 "7-feature ensemble" 作为 Contribution 3（Introduction L21）的分量。论文应更明确地将分类性能降级为 proof-of-concept。
- **建议**：在 Section 4.1 和 Conclusion 中更显式地说：7-feature approach 是 DDR 分析的工具，不是一个竞争性的检测方法

**M4. Baseline 比较存在结构性不公平**
- 具体位置：Table 2 (results.tex L120–139)
- 7-feature（7 个特征）vs 4 个 single-score baselines（各 1 个特征）——这不是公平的苹果对苹果比较
- 实际上 "4-det. + surface"（6 个特征）和 "4-detector ens."（4 个特征）binary F1 = 0.708 和 0.700，**均超过或持平** 7-feature 的 0.705
- 这意味着 DDR-inspired features 在分类性能上并无优势，甚至略逊于 detection score 集成
- 论文在 L150 承认 "DDR's contribution is not classification performance but decomposing depth signal"——但 Table 2 的 presentation 仍给人以 7-feature "胜出" 的印象（行排列中 7-feature 在 3-class F1 上排第三）
- **建议**：(1) 在 Table 2 caption 或正文中明确指出 4-detector ensemble 在 binary F1 上优于 7-feature；(2) 将比较 focus 转向分析解释力（DDR partition）而非分类分数

**M5. Cross-model chain F1=0.830 的评估可能被 generator heterogeneity confound**
- 具体位置：results.tex L12–14, footnote
- 论文承认 "generator heterogeneity in mixed chains may amplify depth-correlated distributional shifts"（L14）
- 作为 counter-evidence 引用了 single-generator transfer F1=0.810（L15），但这是一个不同的设置——train on generator A's single-model chains, test on generator B's single-model chains
- Cross-model chains 中，depth-1 由 generator A 生成、depth-2 由 generator B 生成——distributional shift 混合了 depth effect 和 generator identity，两者共变
- **建议**：在主文中更明确地将 cross-model F1=0.830 标注为 "upper bound under favorable conditions" 而非 depth fingerprinting 的核心性能指标

### Minor

**m1. Bonferroni 校正应用范围不一致**
- results.tex L76: "All p-values are two-sided with Bonferroni correction within each family of simultaneous tests"
- 但 TOST (appendix_tost.tex) 对 8 generators × 7 features = 56 次检验似乎未做 Bonferroni 校正（每个 test 独立 α=0.05）
- KS statistics (results.tex L84): N=29,095 下 KS p≈0 对 **任何** 非零差异都成立——significance 不等于 practical importance，这里 d 值更有信息量

**m2. LOFO 使用 6-generator 子集（appendix_lofo.tex），而非主实验的 8-generator LOGO**
- LOFO baseline F1=0.789 vs 主实验 0.762——数值不直接可比
- 应注明这一差异或在 8-generator 设置下重跑 LOFO

**m3. Entropy_max 的 LOFO 结果与其 DDR 分类矛盾**
- entropy_max 是 near-stationary feature（d=0.08），但 LOFO 中删除它导致最大的 F1 下降（-1.50pp，appendix_lofo.tex Table）
- 这意味着一个 "不随深度变化" 的特征对分类贡献最大——暗示 near-stationary features 可能通过非线性交互（而非直接的深度敏感性）贡献分类
- 值得在正文中讨论这一 apparent paradox

**m4. Temperature sensitivity 的实验边界不够**
- 仅测试 τ ∈ {0.5, 0.7, 0.9}，且 p 固定为 0.9
- 未测试 greedy decoding (τ→0) 或 top-k sampling
- 未测试不同 p 值的 nucleus sampling
- τ=0.9 时 F1 下降 9.3–26.0pp——这是一个很大的范围，说明 DDR 对温度高度敏感

**m5. Orphan bib entry**: `self_refine`（Madaan et al., 2023）存在于 .bib 但未被引用

**m6. Table 2 中 "4-det. + surface" 和 "4-detector ens." 的 feature 组成在 caption 中不够清楚**
- 读者需要回到正文理解这两行的区别
- caption 应自含地解释每个 method 的 feature set

---

## Questions to Authors

**Q1.** 如果将 DDR partition 简化为 2-way（drifting vs. non-drifting），classification performance 会如何变化？具体地说，将 entropy_std 和 entropy_min 从当前分类中移除或重新归组，是否影响下游分类？

**Q2.** Entropy_max 在 LOFO 中贡献最大（-1.50pp），但它是 near-stationary feature——它如何通过 depth 不相关的信号帮助分类？是否通过与 drifting features 的非线性交互起作用？

**Q3.** Per-generator TOST 中 tail_decay 仅 4/8 通过（ε=0.20）。如果将 tail_decay 重分类为 intermediate（与 entropy_std 一起），partition 变为 3/2/2——论文的主要结论是否仍然成立？

**Q4.** Cross-model chain 实验中，是否可以控制 generator heterogeneity confound？例如，构建 "depth-1 和 depth-2 都用同一个 generator，但 depth-0 来自不同 generator" 的链，以隔离 depth effect。

**Q5.** Downstream experiment（Appendix M）显示 depth-aware curation 不如 random subsampling——这是否意味着 depth fingerprinting 的唯一用途是分析性的（理解 DDR），而非实用性的（改善数据质量）？

**Q6.** 7-feature approach 在 instruct data 上 LOGO F1=0.487（near chance），而 QLoRA 恢复到 0.89。这是否说明 7 个 summary statistics 从根本上无法捕获 instruct model 的 depth signal？如果是，DDR 的 drifting/stationary decomposition 在 instruct 模型上是否仍然有意义？

---

## Missing References

1. **Guo et al. (2024)** "On the Stability of Iterative Retraining of Generative Models on their own Data" (ICLR 2024) — 直接研究迭代生成链的分布收敛，与 DDR 的 location/shape 分解高度相关
2. **Li et al. (2024)** "Self-Consuming Generative Models with Curated Data Provably Optimize Human Preferences" — 理论分析递归生成中的分布演化，可加强 Discussion 中 DDR 与 model collapse 的联系
3. **Zhang et al. (2024)** "Detecting Machine-Generated Texts by Multi-Population Aware Optimization for Maximum Mean Discrepancy" — MMD-based detection 方法，可作为额外 baseline 参照

---

## Overall Assessment

**Overall**: 3.5 / 5 — Borderline Conference

| 维度 | 分数 | 理由 |
|------|------|------|
| Soundness | 3.5/5 | 2-way DDR split 有扎实支持，但 3/1/3 refinement 是 post-hoc 构建；entropy_min 分类矛盾；tail_decay TOST 仅 50% 通过 |
| Excitement | 3/5 | 任务新颖，DDR insight 有价值；但实际分类性能中等，QLoRA 证明 7-feature 是 lossy compression，downstream utility 为 null |
| Reproducibility | 4/5 | 极为详细的实验描述（hyperparameters、seeds、model versions），code/data 承诺公开 |
| Datasets | 3/5 | 37K 样本、8 generators、单一 domain（Wikipedia），未公开 |
| Software | 2/5 | 未公开（承诺 upon publication） |
| Reviewer Confidence | 4/5 | 熟悉 AI text detection、统计检验方法、ordinal classification |

**核心判断**：论文的最大价值在于 DDR 的二元分解（drifting vs. non-drifting features），这是一个 clean 且跨生成器一致的发现。但论文的 framing 过度推进到了 3/1/3 partition——这个 granularity 超出了数据支持的范围，依赖 domain-informed override 而非 data-driven evidence。

如果作者能够：(1) 以 2-way split 为核心、3/1/3 为 secondary analysis；(2) 更诚实地处理 tail_decay 和 entropy_min 的 borderline 状态；(3) 将分类性能明确定位为 proof-of-concept 而非 practical contribution——论文的 soundness 将显著提升，可达 4.0（Conference）。当前状态 3.5，适合 Borderline Conference 或 strong Findings。

## Reviewer 2 审稿报告 — Round 1

**Overall Assessment**: 3.0 — Findings
**Confidence**: 4/5

### Must-Fix 问题

**N1** [critical] 仅限 Base Model 的实验设计严重削弱论文的现实意义
- 所有实验仅使用 base model，现实中几乎所有 LLM 生成文本来自 instruction-tuned 或 RLHF 模型。Appendix K 显示 instruct 下 F1 下降 3.7–19.9pp。标题暗示通用性但实际仅适用于 base model。

**N2** [critical] DDR 发现的增量新颖性不清晰——与已知 LLM 多样性损失的区分不足
- DDR 核心（中心趋势漂移+形状稳定）可能只是 diversity loss / mode-seeking behavior 的重新表述。Geng et al. (2026) 已展示 attractor dynamics bounding depth to ~3 classes。论文需证明 DDR 的 location/shape 分解提供了哪些已有文献未涵盖的 insights。

**N3** [critical] 核心分类性能偏低，实用性论证不充分
- Binary F1=0.694，cross-model F1=0.830 引入了额外 signal。Downstream utility TOST 检验证明 depth-aware 和 random curation 无显著差异。分类性能不足以支撑实际应用。

### Should-Fix 问题

**W1** [major] 遗漏直接相关的重要工作：Wang et al. (ACL 2025) "Unveiling Attractor Cycles in LLMs"，Sun et al. (2026) "When AI Settles Down"

**W2** [major] 术语混淆："entropy" 作为 NLL 的简称不规范，应改为 "nll_X" 或 "surprisal_X"

**W3** [major] 附录过于庞大（25 页），关键结果（Appendix K instruct、Appendix E QLoRA）应在主文讨论

**W4** [major] 主文缺少神经网络基线对比，QLoRA 被完全放在附录中

**W5** [minor] Abstract 中 cross-model F1=0.830 与 LOGO F1=0.694 并列有误导

**W6** [minor] Figure 2 黑白打印不可辨别

### Questions
1. 如何回应"DDR 只是 mode-seeking behavior / diversity loss 的重新表述"？
2. DDR 在 instruct models 上是完全消失还是 attenuated？
3. Cross-model F1=0.830 如何排除 generator heterogeneity 作为分类信号？
4. Downstream utility TOST 显示无显著差异——depth fingerprinting 有 actionable value 吗？

### Missing References
1. Wang et al. (ACL 2025) "Unveiling Attractor Cycles in LLMs"
2. Sun et al. (2026) "When AI Settles Down" arXiv:2601.04833
3. Orphan bib: self_refine (Madaan et al., 2023)

input.text:
## Reviewer 1 对 Reviewer 2 Round 1 意见的逐条回应

---

### Must-Fix 问题

**[AGREE] R2-N1: 仅限 Base Model 的实验设计严重削弱现实意义**

同意。这也是我自己审稿中提出的核心问题。Appendix K（Table 11）数据非常明确：OLMo-2-1B-Instruct 3-class F1 从 0.754 跌至 0.575（-17.9pp），Llama-3.2-3B-Instruct 从 0.742 跌至 0.544（-19.8pp）。更关键的是 Appendix K 最后的 DDR 结构分析：instruct 模型上 k=2 clustering silhouette 从 0.632 降至 0.338，说明 DDR 的 drifting/non-drifting 分解本身在 instruct 模型上被压缩。论文 abstract 最后一句 "current applicability is restricted to base models" 虽然诚实，但标题 "LLM Text Chains" 仍暗示通用性。

不过需要补充一点：Appendix K 的 QLoRA 在 instruct 数据上 3-class F1 恢复到 0.888–0.907（Table 13），说明 depth signal 在 token level 仍然存在，只是 7 个 summary statistics 无法捕获 instruct 模型的 depth 特征。这支持论文的辩护方向（L82–83: "degradation reported in Table 11 reflects a feature-level limitation rather than signal absence"），但也进一步说明 7-feature DDR 方法在 instruct 场景下基本失效。

**[REBUT] R2-N2: DDR 只是 diversity loss / mode-seeking behavior 的重新表述**

不完全同意。R2 的批评指向一个真实的 concern——DDR 的 drifting component（entropy mean, TTR, hapax ratio 下降）确实对应已知的 diversity loss 现象。但 DDR 的核心贡献不是 "递归生成导致多样性下降"（这确实是已知的），而是 **分解出一类在递归中保持稳定的特征**。

具体证据：
1. **Shape stability 是新发现**。Geng et al. (2026) [markovian_chains] 证明 attractor dynamics bounding depth to ~3 classes，但他们分析的是 aggregate convergence，没有区分哪些分布属性收敛、哪些不收敛。DDR 的 near-stationary component（entropy max d=0.08, tail decay d=0.08）文献中没有对应的发现。
2. **Decomposition 的诊断价值**。Section 6 (discussion.tex L4–7) 提供了一个 mechanism 解释：nucleus sampling 的 top-p truncation 保留条件分布的 shape，同时 input 的 self-typicality 递增导致 location drift。这不是 diversity loss 的重新表述，而是对 diversity loss 的 **机制分解**。
3. **Shape stability 使 depth detection 成为可能**。论文明确指出（results.tex L150）："DDR's contribution is not classification performance but decomposing depth signal into location-sensitive and shape-stable components"。没有 shape stability baseline，location drift 就无法被测量。

然而，我认为论文应该更 prominently 地与 Geng et al. (2026) 和 Mohamed et al. (2025) [broken_telephone] 做 explicit comparison，说明："他们展示了 X，我们补充了 Y（shape stability + mechanism decomposition）"。当前 related work（Section 2.2）引用了这两篇但没有做足够细致的区分。

**[AGREE with nuance] R2-N3: 核心分类性能偏低**

部分同意。Binary F1=0.694 确实不足以支撑 "practical depth classifier" 的定位（Introduction L21, Contribution 3）。Appendix L (Table 18) 显示 overall error rate 28.08%，depth-2 samples 的 error rate 高达 48.42%。

但需要 nuance：
- 论文已在 results.tex L150 和 discussion.tex L12 做了明确定位——DDR 是分析工具而非部署方案
- Discussion L12 提到 "Document-level gen-1 per-class F1=0.63 is insufficient for automated filtering but sufficient for corpus-level flagging"——这是一个合理的 use case 区分
- 我在自己的审稿中也建议将分类性能明确降级为 proof-of-concept（我的 M3）

R2 关于 downstream TOST 的批评完全正确：Appendix M (Table 17) 显示 random subsampling (2.367) 优于 depth-aware curation (2.387)——depth fingerprinting 对数据清洗无正面效果。论文自己也承认这是 null result（appendix_downstream.tex L22: "The results are unambiguous: data quantity dominates depth composition"）。

---

### Should-Fix 问题

**[REBUT] R2-W1: 遗漏 Wang et al. (ACL 2025) "Unveiling Attractor Cycles in LLMs" 和 Sun et al. (2026)**

我无法确认这两篇论文的存在。"Wang et al. (ACL 2025) Unveiling Attractor Cycles in LLMs" 和 "Sun et al. (2026) When AI Settles Down (arXiv:2601.04833)" 需要 R2 提供确切的引用信息以便验证。论文已经引用了该领域最相关的两篇工作——Geng et al. (2026) [markovian_chains] 和 Mohamed et al. (2025) [broken_telephone]——它们直接研究 LLM 生成链中的 attractor dynamics 和信息退化。如果 R2 引用的论文确实存在且内容不同，应补充；但不应基于未经验证的引用判定为 "遗漏重要工作"。

**[AGREE with qualification] R2-W2: "entropy" 术语混淆**

论文在 method.tex L39 已做了明确说明："We use 'entropy' as shorthand for token-level NLL throughout, following convention in prior detection work; these are point-wise NLL values, not Shannon entropy of the full distribution." 这个 convention 在 AI text detection 文献中确实常见（如 DetectGPT, Binoculars 等都用类似简写），但 R2 说得对——对于不在这个子领域的读者，"entropy_mean" 容易误解为 "Shannon entropy 的均值"。

建议折中方案：保留 "entropy" shorthand 但在首次出现时加脚注，或在 feature 定义表中同时标注 formal name（NLL mean）和 shorthand（entropy_mean）。全面改名为 "nll_X" 或 "surprisal_X" 代价过大且与该领域 convention 不一致。

**[REBUT] R2-W3: 附录过于庞大（25 页）**

不同意这是一个 weakness。ARR review form 明确说明 "reviewers are not required to read the appendix"——附录的存在不增加 reviewer 负担。相反，论文将关键但详细的验证（TOST、holdout split、bootstrap、Granger causality 等）放在附录中，正是为了保持主文 8 页的精简。

我在自己的审稿中将附录的彻底性列为主要优势（S5）。25+ 个子节覆盖了几乎所有合理的 robustness check，这在 EMNLP 投稿中罕见且值得肯定。如果将 Appendix K（instruct）和 E（QLoRA）的核心数字搬入主文（见 W4 的讨论），附录本身的存在不是问题。

**[AGREE] R2-W4: 主文缺少神经网络基线对比，QLoRA 应在主文讨论**

同意。QLoRA 是理解论文贡献边界的关键实验：
- 它证明 depth signal 远超 7 个 handcrafted features 能捕获的范围（+11.6pp）
- 它在 instruct 数据上恢复到 0.89–0.91，证明 depth signal 的 token-level 持续性
- 它为 "DDR 是分析贡献而非分类贡献" 的定位提供了最强证据

当前 results.tex L19 仅用一句话提到 QLoRA（"An end-to-end QLoRA classifier achieves 3-class F1=0.905"）。建议至少将 Appendix E Table 6 的核心数字和 Appendix K Table 13 的 instruct QLoRA 结果纳入 Section 4.1 或 Section 6，用 2-3 句话解释其对 contribution 定位的影响。

**[AGREE] R2-W5: Abstract 中 cross-model F1=0.830 与 LOGO F1=0.694 并列有误导**

同意。Abstract (abstract.tex L5) 写 "binary F1=0.694 (95% CI [.688, .700]) under leave-one-generator-out evaluation and 0.830 on cross-model chains (5-generator subset, LOGO)"——虽然标注了 "5-generator subset"，但两个数字并列仍暗示这是同一尺度上的递进。

论文自己在 results.tex L14 承认 "The higher cross-model binary F1 relative to the 8-generator LOGO (0.694) is not directly comparable"。Abstract 应更清楚地传达这一点——例如将 0.830 移到括号注释或在 abstract 中省略，仅在主文中报告。

**[REBUT] R2-W6: Figure 2 黑白打印不可辨别**

论文中 Figure 2 是 DDR trajectory plot（fig_ddr_trajectory.pdf），显示 4 个 feature 在不同 depth 下的轨迹。从 PDF 渲染（page 5）看，该图使用了 bold black line（cross-generator mean）+ thin colored lines（individual generators），主要信息（drifting vs. flat）通过 y-axis 趋势传达，而非颜色区分。黑白打印下，drifting panels 的明显下降趋势 vs. stationary panels 的平坦走势仍然清晰。EMNLP/ARR 审稿和最终发表均为电子版（PDF），黑白打印兼容性不是 ARR 的强制要求。

---

### Questions 回应

**R2-Q1: "DDR 只是 mode-seeking behavior 的重新表述？"**
见上方 N2 的 [REBUT]。核心回应：drifting component 对应已知的 diversity loss，但 shape stability 是新发现，mechanism decomposition（location shift at stable shape via nucleus truncation）是新的理论贡献。

**R2-Q2: "DDR 在 instruct models 上完全消失还是 attenuated？"**
根据 Appendix K：是 attenuated 而非消失。具体地：
- Binary F1（gen-1 vs gen-2+）变化较小（|Δ| ≤ 3.2pp，Table 11）——说明 gen-1/gen-2+ 区分仍有微弱 signal
- 但 feature polarity 反转（6/7 features 的 ρ 符号翻转），说明 DDR 的 direction 改变了
- k=2 silhouette 从 0.632 降至 0.338——说明 partition structure 被压缩但未完全消除
- QLoRA 在 instruct 上 F1=0.888–0.907——说明 token-level depth signal 仍然强

结论：DDR 的 summary-statistic 版本在 instruct 上严重 attenuated 且方向翻转；但 depth signal 在 token level 持续存在。

**R2-Q3: "Cross-model F1=0.830 如何排除 generator heterogeneity？"**
同意这是一个 valid concern。我在自己的审稿中也提出了这一点（M5）。论文提供了 partial evidence——single-generator transfer F1=0.810（results.tex L15）——但这是 different setup。Cross-model chains 中 depth 和 generator identity 共变，无法完全分离。论文应将 0.830 更保守地呈现为 upper bound。

**R2-Q4: "Downstream utility TOST 显示无显著差异——depth fingerprinting 有 actionable value 吗？"**
同意 downstream utility 是 null result（见我的 M2）。论文的 actionable value 主要在分析层面（理解递归生成的分布变化机制）和 corpus-level auditing（Discussion L12–13），而非 sample-level filtering 或数据清洗。论文应更明确地定位这一点。

---

### Missing References 回应

**Wang et al. (ACL 2025) 和 Sun et al. (2026)**：无法确认这两篇论文的存在（见 W1 回应）。需要 R2 提供确切信息以便验证。

**Orphan bib self_refine**：[AGREE] 确认存在，应删除或补充引用。我在自己的审稿中也指出了这一点。

---

### 总结

R2 审稿整体合理，但我认为有两处评价偏严：
1. **N2（DDR 新颖性）**：R2 低估了 shape stability 发现的增量价值。DDR 不是 diversity loss 的重新表述——它分解出了一个之前未被 documented 的 near-stationary component，这对理解 recursive generation mechanism 有独立价值。
2. **W3（附录过大）**：附录的彻底性是优势而非劣势，尤其在 reviewer 不必须阅读附录的 ARR 政策下。

其他问题（N1 base-model-only, N3 分类性能, W4 QLoRA 位置, W5 abstract misleading）我大体同意 R2 的判断。

综合两份审稿，我维持 **3.5（Borderline Conference）** 的评分。论文的 DDR 二元分解是 genuine insight，评估极为彻底，但 base-model 限制和 3/1/3 partition 的 over-claiming 阻碍了 conference 接收。如果修改后能以 2-way split 为核心、将分类降级为 proof-of-concept，并明确 instruct 限制，可达 Findings 或 Borderline Conference。

1	\section{Results}
2	\label{sec:results}
3	
4	\subsection{Depth Classification Performance}
5	\label{sec:results-classification}
6	
7	Before analyzing the DDR decomposition (\S\ref{sec:results-differential}), we establish that generation depth is classifiable across diverse architectures.
8	The 7-feature ensemble achieves 3-class LOGO F1\,=\,0.762 (95\% CI [0.758, 0.766]; $N$\,=\,37{,}058) across eight generators from five families (Table~\ref{tab:logo-results}).
9	Because gen-0 seeds are shared across generators (\S\ref{sec:generation}), gen-0 classification is near-perfect (per-class F1\,$\approx$\,0.94), inflating the 3-class metric.
10	We therefore adopt \textbf{leak-free binary F1} (gen-1 vs.\ gen-2+)\,=\,0.694 (CI [0.688, 0.700]) as the primary metric throughout: it excludes gen-0 entirely and is unaffected by seed sharing.
11	Per-generator binary F1 ranges from 0.633 (Mistral-7B) to 0.724 (Pythia-2.8B), with the primary difficulty concentrated at the gen-1\,/\,gen-2+ boundary (Appendix~\ref{app:confusion}).
12	
13	\paragraph{Cross-model generalization.}
14	Cross-model chains (randomly selected generator per step) yield binary F1\,=\,0.830 (95\% CI [.818, .841]) under 5-generator LOGO.\footnote{5-generator subset (Pythia-2.8B/1B, OLMo-2-1B, Qwen3-0.6B/1.7B); generator-level LOGO with bootstrap CIs ($n$\,=\,2{,}000). Not directly comparable to 8-generator LOGO due to differing subsets.}
15	Single-generator transfer (Appendix~\ref{app:transfer}) confirms the signal is not a mixed-chain artifact: classifiers trained on one generator transfer to all others with mean binary F1\,=\,0.810; LOFO yields 0.686.
16	A scale effect emerges: Pythia achieves the highest F1 (0.718--0.724) while larger models degrade (Mistral-7B: 0.633), partly reflecting same-family affinity with the Pythia-410M reference (cross-reference spread $\leq$0.013; \S\ref{sec:results-differential}); cross-domain signal persists with variation (Appendix~\ref{app:domain}).
17	An end-to-end QLoRA classifier ($+$11.6\,pp, 3-class F1\,=\,0.905; Appendix~\ref{app:qlora}) confirms that richer representations capture additional depth signal; on instruct data, QLoRA recovers to 0.89--0.91 (Appendix~\ref{app:instruct}), establishing the empirical decomposition---not the specific classifier---as DDR's primary contribution.
18	
19	\paragraph{Length confound control.}
20	Length-matched subsampling yields binary F1\,=\,0.724 (vs.\ 0.770 unmatched); a random-subsample control confirms the drop reflects deconfounding, not sample-size reduction (Appendix~\ref{app:length}).
21	
22	\paragraph{Seed-sharing control.}
23	Seed-level demeaning (F1\,=\,0.701) and an independent-seed experiment with disjoint seed pools (F1\,=\,0.680; Appendix~\ref{app:seed-control}) both confirm the classifier captures generative degradation, not seed-specific content.
24	
25	\begin{table}[t]
26	\centering
27	\footnotesize
28	\resizebox{\columnwidth}{!}{%
29	\begin{tabular}{llcccc}
30	\toprule
31	\textbf{Model} & \textbf{Family} & \textbf{Params} & \textbf{Bin F1} & \textbf{95\% CI} & \textbf{3-cl F1}$^{\dagger}$ \\

Binary F1 (gen-1 vs.\ gen-2+) is the primary metric; it excludes gen-0 entirely and is unaffected by seed sharing. $^{\dagger}$3-class F1 carries upward bias because gen-0 seeds are shared across generators (\S\ref{sec:generation}); independent-seed controls confirm the depth signal (F1\,=\,0.680; Appendix~\ref{app:seed-control}).}
47	\label{tab:logo-results}

50	\subsection{Differential Depth Response}
51	\label{sec:results-differential}
52	
53	\begin{figure*}[t]
54	\centering
55	\includegraphics[width=\textwidth]{fig_ddr_trajectory.pdf}
56	\caption{Feature trajectories across generation depth. \textbf{Top row (drifting)}: entropy mean and hapax ratio decline monotonically across all eight generators ($|\rho| > 0.59$). \textbf{Bottom row (stationary)}: entropy max and tail decay remain flat ($|\rho| < 0.07$). Colored lines: individual generators; diamonds: cross-generator mean (blue for drifting, amber for stationary). This dichotomy defines the differential depth response (DDR).}
57	\label{fig:ddr-trajectory}
58	\end{figure*}
59	
60	Not all distributional properties respond equally to recursive generation.
61	Figure~\ref{fig:ddr-trajectory} reveals a striking dichotomy that holds across all eight generators: central-tendency features (entropy mean, TTR, hapax ratio) decline monotonically with depth, while shape features (entropy max, tail decay, entropy min) remain flat.
62	We term this asymmetry the \emph{differential depth response} (DDR).
63	The primary partition is binary: $k{=}2$ clustering in standardized $(|\rho|, d)$ space yields silhouette\,=\,0.632 (Appendix~\ref{app:ddr-validation}), cleanly separating three \emph{drifting} features ($|\rho| > 0.60$, $d{=}0.76$--$1.17$) from four \emph{non-drifting} ones ($d \leq 0.55$); higher $k$ degrades cluster quality ($k{=}3$: silhouette\,=\,0.499).
64	A domain-informed refinement resolves entropy std as a sole \emph{intermediate} member ($d{=}0.55$, $|\rho|{=}0.16$), distinct from the three near-stationary features ($d < 0.10$; CV shift $<$3\% vs.\ $>$15\% for drifting features).
65	Five independent effect-size metrics converge on this drifting/non-drifting partition, confirming that the location/shape asymmetry reflects distributional structure rather than feature-selection artifact.
66	
67	\begin{figure}[t]
68	\centering
69	\includegraphics[width=\columnwidth]{fig1_differential_response.pdf}
70	\caption{Differential depth response (DDR). Diamonds: cross-generator means; dots: per-generator values. Drifting features (blue; $|\rho| > 0.60$, $d{=}0.76$--$1.17$) show strong monotonic depth sensitivity; non-drifting features remain stable. Entropy std (wine; $d{=}0.55$) is an intermediate member; three near-stationary features (amber; $d < 0.10$) show negligible drift. Entropy min ($|\rho|{=}0.40$ pooled) is a boundary feature whose sensitivity concentrates at the gen-0/gen-1 transition.}
71	\label{fig:feature-drift}
72	\end{figure}
73	
74	Pooled class-balanced Spearman correlations with depth confirm the binary split (Figure~\ref{fig:feature-drift}):
75	drifting features show substantial monotonic trends (hapax ratio $\rho = -0.64$, TTR $\rho = -0.63$, entropy mean $\rho = -0.60$),
76	while non-drifting features remain near-zero (tail decay $|\rho| = 0.04$; per-depth distributions in Appendix~\ref{app:feature-distributions}).
77	The six-fold magnitude gap between drifting ($|\rho| > 0.60$) and non-drifting features ($|\rho| \leq 0.16$) defines the DDR partition.
78	Within the non-drifting group, entropy std ($|\rho| = 0.16$, $d{=}0.55$) shows a substantial level shift despite low monotonicity, distinguishing it from the three near-stationary features ($d < 0.10$); this refinement is stable across $d$ thresholds in $[0.56, 0.75]$ (Appendix~\ref{app:ddr-validation}).
79	
80	\paragraph{Quantification.}
81	Every tested effect-size metric confirms the split.
82	Cohen's $d$ \cite{cohen1988statistical} converges with $\rho$: drifting features show large effects ($d{=}0.76$--$1.17$) while shape features are near zero ($d \leq 0.08$); KS statistics show a ${\sim}10\times$ gap (0.516--0.537 vs.\ 0.043--0.052; all $p \approx 0$).
83	Glass's $\Delta$ and Cliff's $\delta$ corroborate the partition with a ${\geq}9.5\times$ gap; CV shift ($<$3\% vs.\ $>$15\%) supports ``near-stationary'' as a practical characterization (Appendix~\ref{app:ddr-validation}).
84	Five features fall cleanly into drifting or non-drifting groups; the remaining two require qualification.
85	Entropy min is a \emph{boundary feature}: its gen-1 vs.\ gen-2+ effect is near-stationary ($d{=}0.016$) despite a substantial pooled $|\rho|$ (0.40) driven by the gen-0/gen-1 transition (Cliff's $\delta{=}0.354$ confirms shape change without location shift); $k{=}2$ clustering places it with non-drifting features (Appendix~\ref{app:ddr-validation}).
86	Entropy std shows a substantial level shift ($d{=}0.55$) despite low monotonicity ($|\rho|{=}0.16$), making it the sole intermediate feature.
87	\paragraph{Validation.}
88	The partition is not a pooling artifact.
89	Per-generator TOST equivalence testing ($\varepsilon{=}|d|{<}0.20$, gen-1 vs.\ gen-2+) confirms stability for entropy min (8/8 generators pass) and entropy max (6/8); tail decay passes for only 4/8 generators, with OLMo-2-1B ($d{=}0.22$) exceeding the equivalence bound (Appendix~\ref{app:tost}).
90	Bootstrap resampling (1{,}000 iterations) on the pooled sample achieves 100\% rejection for all three near-stationary features, but high pooled power ($N \approx 3{,}500$--$4{,}500$ per generator) can mask per-generator heterogeneity.
91	Tail decay's 50\% per-generator pass rate represents a genuine boundary case: reclassifying it as intermediate preserves the core drifting/non-drifting split and classification performance (F1 change $<$0.5\,pp).
92	
93	\paragraph{Feature complementarity.}
94	The full 7-feature set (F1\,=\,0.773) outperforms surface-only (0.688) and reference-only (0.713; McNemar $p \approx 0$; Appendix~\ref{app:ablation-table}).
95	PCA confirms the three drifting features share a single latent dimension (92.3\% variance; Appendix~\ref{sec:appendix-feature-correlation}); replacing them with PC1 costs only 1.1\,pp, confirming that DDR's contribution is identifying \emph{which} distributional properties drift, not classification per se.
96	TTR and hapax ratio ($r = 0.97$) are both retained for marginal LOFO gains despite feature masking \cite{strobl_conditional_2008} (Appendix~\ref{app:lofo}).
97	
98	\paragraph{Cross-family reference models.}
99	Alternative references (OLMo-2-1B, Qwen3-0.6B) achieve comparable LOGO F1 (spread 0.013; Appendix~\ref{app:cross-ref}), bounding the same-family affinity effect; depth features are robust to reference model choice.
100	
101	\paragraph{Temperature and prompt-type sensitivity.}
102	All four tested generators degrade at $t{=}0.9$ ($-9.3$ to $-26.0$\,pp binary F1); low-temperature improvement is family-dependent ($+7$--$9$\,pp for Pythia/OLMo at $t{=}0.5$, negligible for Qwen; Appendix~\ref{app:sampling-sensitivity}).
103	Continuation chains show the strongest drift (F1\,=\,0.781), with cross-prompt-type transfer confirming shared signal (LOPTO F1\,=\,0.753; Appendix~\ref{app:prompt-type}); the DDR partition hierarchy is preserved across temperatures despite absolute effect-size compression (Appendix~\ref{app:ddr-temp-stability}).
104	
105	
106	\subsection{Comparison with Detection Baselines}
107	\label{sec:results-baselines}
108	
109	Existing detection methods target binary real-vs-synthetic classification; their continuous scores encode distributional divergence that may incidentally correlate with recursive depth.
110	To test this, we repurpose four detection scores as ordinal depth predictors under identical XGBoost and LOGO conditions (Table~\ref{tab:baselines}).

Identical XGBoost configuration. 7-feature: one 410M model (905\,MB); 4-det ensembles: two models, 1.4B params (2{,}868\,MB). Individual detection scores (N/A) share the reference-model forward pass; per-method timing is not separately profiled.}

132	
133	\begin{figure}[t]

137	\label{fig:baseline-ci}
138	\end{figure}
139	
140	The 7-feature ensemble surpasses all individual baselines in 3-class F1 ($\Delta$\,=\,6.7--36.3\,pp; Figure~\ref{fig:baseline-ci}) and the pure 4-detector ensemble in binary F1 (0.705 vs.\ 0.700).
141	Adding DDR's surface features to the four detectors yields the highest binary F1 (0.708), marginally above the 7-feature set at 2.4$\times$ the inference cost.
