1	\section{Introduction}
2	\label{sec:introduction}
3	
4	AI text detection asks a single binary question---\emph{human or machine?}---and recent methods answer it with increasing reliability \cite{detectgpt,fast_detectgpt,binoculars,ld_score}.
5	Yet this framing elides a richer structure emerging on the open web: as LLM outputs re-enter training corpora \cite{dolma,fineweb} and seed further generation, text accumulates at varying \emph{recursive depths}---an estimated 7--17\% of recent scientific publications already contain substantial LLM-modified content \cite{mapping_llm_science,monitoring_ai_review}---and each generation cycle pushes distributional properties further from both the human source and the first-generation predecessor.
6	Knowing \emph{how many times} text has been recursively generated matters for data provenance \cite{ccnet,dsir} and model collapse analysis \cite{curse_of_recursion,strong_model_collapse}, yet no current method moves beyond the binary boundary.
7	
8	We introduce \emph{depth fingerprinting}: classifying text by ordinal generation depth (gen-0\,/\,gen-1\,/\,gen-2+) and decomposing the distributional drift that accumulates across depths into structurally distinct components.
9	The core empirical finding is a \emph{differential depth response} (DDR): across eight base-model generators spanning five architectural families (0.6B--8B), the NLL distribution's central tendency (mean entropy, lexical diversity) drifts monotonically with depth while its shape (entropy extremes, tail structure) remains an order of magnitude more stable ($d{=}0.76$--$1.17$ vs.\ $d < 0.10$; five independent effect-size metrics converge on this partition).
10	This location/shape asymmetry exposes a structural property of fixed-parameter autoregressive sampling: the decoding mechanism systematically compresses where the output distribution sits while preserving its higher-order form---a pattern mechanistically distinct from the tail-coverage erosion in model collapse \cite{curse_of_recursion}, and analytically informative independent of classification accuracy.
11	Concurrent work characterizes convergence in paraphrastic and translation chains \cite{broken_telephone,markovian_chains}; ours is the first to decompose the drift into complementary location and shape components and to leverage this asymmetry for cross-generator depth prediction.
12	We restrict to base (pretrained) models to isolate the generation dynamics from alignment artifacts (\S\ref{sec:discussion}).
13	
14	As a proof of concept, a lightweight 7-feature ensemble informed by DDR achieves binary F1\,=\,0.694 under leave-one-generator-out evaluation and 0.830 on heterogeneous cross-model chains, surpassing individual detection baselines by 6.7--36.3\,pp while requiring 2.4$\times$ less inference cost than multi-detector ensembles of comparable accuracy.
15	
16	Our contributions:
17	\begin{enumerate}[nosep,leftmargin=*]
18	    \item \textbf{Empirical decomposition (DDR).} Data-driven clustering ($k{=}2$, silhouette\,=\,0.632) reveals that inference-chain drift separates into a drifting location component ($d{=}0.76$--$1.17$) and a stable shape component ($d < 0.10$). Where prior work documents \emph{what converges}, DDR identifies \emph{what is preserved}---enabling depth detection without per-generator calibration.
19	    \item \textbf{Task formulation and evaluation suite.} We define generation depth classification as an ordinal prediction task and construct a controlled dataset of 37K texts from eight generators across five families (0.6B--8B), with leave-one-generator-out cross-validation as the primary evaluation protocol.
20	    \item \textbf{Proof-of-concept classifier with boundary analysis.} A 7-feature ensemble achieves binary F1\,=\,0.830 on cross-model chains; we systematically map its operating boundaries across temperature, prompt type, instruction tuning, and model scale.
21	\end{enumerate}

\section{Introduction}
\label{sec:introduction}

AI text detection asks a single binary question---\emph{human or machine?}---and recent methods answer it with increasing reliability \cite{detectgpt,fast_detectgpt,binoculars,ld_score}.
Yet this framing elides a richer structure emerging on the open web: as LLM outputs re-enter training corpora \cite{dolma,fineweb} and seed further generation, text accumulates at varying \emph{recursive depths}---an estimated 7--17\% of recent scientific publications already contain substantial LLM-modified content \cite{mapping_llm_science,monitoring_ai_review}---and each generation cycle pushes distributional properties further from both the human source and the first-generation predecessor.
Knowing \emph{how many times} text has been recursively generated matters for data provenance \cite{ccnet,dsir} and model collapse analysis \cite{curse_of_recursion,strong_model_collapse}, yet no current method moves beyond the binary boundary.

We introduce \emph{depth fingerprinting}: classifying text by ordinal generation depth (gen-0\,/\,gen-1\,/\,gen-2+) and decomposing the distributional drift that accumulates across depths into structurally distinct components.
The core empirical finding is a \emph{differential depth response} (DDR): across eight base-model generators spanning five architectural families (0.6B--8B), the NLL distribution's central tendency (mean entropy, lexical diversity) drifts monotonically with depth while its shape (entropy extremes, tail structure) remains an order of magnitude more stable ($d{=}0.76$--$1.17$ vs.\ $d < 0.10$; five independent effect-size metrics converge on this partition).
This location/shape asymmetry exposes a structural property of fixed-parameter autoregressive sampling: the decoding mechanism systematically compresses where the output distribution sits while preserving its higher-order form---a pattern mechanistically distinct from the tail-coverage erosion in model collapse \cite{curse_of_recursion}, and analytically informative independent of classification accuracy.
Concurrent work characterizes convergence in paraphrastic and translation chains \cite{broken_telephone,markovian_chains}; ours is the first to decompose the drift into complementary location and shape components and to leverage this asymmetry for cross-generator depth prediction.
We restrict to base (pretrained) models to isolate the generation dynamics from alignment artifacts (\S\ref{sec:discussion}).

1	\section{Discussion}
2	\label{sec:discussion}
3	
4	Recursive generation alters \emph{where} the token-level surprise distribution sits but not \emph{how} it is shaped---a dichotomy that admits a mechanistic interpretation.
5	Under nucleus sampling, top-$p$ truncation selects from a fixed probability-mass fraction at each step, preserving the functional form of the conditional distribution regardless of input content.
6	What changes across recursive steps is the \emph{input} to this truncation: as the model conditions on its own increasingly self-typical outputs, the expected token-level NLL compresses monotonically---each generation feeds slightly more predictable input into the same shape-preserving mechanism.
7	This account yields two testable predictions: (1)~increasing sampling randomness should weaken the location drift by disrupting mode-seeking, and (2)~semantic-preservation constraints should attenuate it by anchoring the input distribution.
8	Both are empirically confirmed: at $t{=}1.0$, the location signal collapses ($\rho$: $-0.60 \to -0.002$; Appendix~\ref{app:sampling-sensitivity}); under elaboration prompts, drift weakens relative to continuation (F1\,=\,0.730 vs.\ 0.781; Appendix~\ref{app:prompt-type}), consistent with \citet{broken_telephone}, while cross-type transfer remains viable (F1\,=\,0.753).
9	Permutation importance, Granger causality, and feature intervention analyses provide further causal evidence: drifting features contribute $5.5\times$ more to classification than near-stationary ones, with 6/7 features exhibiting significant Granger causality (Appendix~\ref{app:ddr-causality}).
10	
11	The classifier is a proof-of-concept, not a deployable system: document-level gen-1 per-class F1\,=\,0.63 and ${\sim}30\%$ error rate are insufficient for automated filtering but sufficient for corpus-level flagging ($O(1/\sqrt{n})$ error scaling), with the primary difficulty being gen-1 vs.\ gen-2+ discrimination (86\% false negatives; Appendix~\ref{app:error-analysis}).
12	Practical utility lies in batch auditing (gen-2+ proportion thresholds) and provenance tracing (seed-lineage reconstruction).
13	In generator-unknown deployment, LOGO F1\,=\,0.694 provides a conservative lower bound (9.1\,pp per-generator spread); cross-temperature transfer degrades when test-time temperature exceeds training (F1\,$\to$\,0.723; Appendix~\ref{app:cross-temp}).
14	
15	Preliminary evidence from a 14.7B generator (Qwen3-14B-Base) confirms that the DDR partition persists at larger scale: Cohen's $d$ for drifting features remains in the large-effect range ($d{=}0.78$--$1.12$), though Spearman $|\rho|$ attenuates by 21--35\%, with entropy mean approaching the drifting boundary ($|\rho|{=}0.39$, $d{=}0.78$).
16	This scale-dependent signal compression is consistent with larger models producing more self-typical outputs that narrow inter-depth contrasts; the partition structure is preserved even as absolute effect sizes compress.
17	
18	DDR connects to but is mechanistically distinct from model collapse \cite{curse_of_recursion,strong_model_collapse}: retraining permanently erodes tail coverage by updating model weights, whereas inference-chain drift at fixed parameters shifts only the NLL distribution's location, leaving its shape as a stable reference.
19	Prior work documents \emph{what converges}---diversity loss \cite{curious_decline}, attractor dynamics \cite{markovian_chains}, mode collapse \cite{curse_of_recursion}---but not what is \emph{preserved}; this complementary observation is what enables depth detection without per-generator calibration.
20	Three depth classes represent the practical resolution ceiling (5-class F1\,$\approx$\,0.50; Appendix~\ref{app:finer-depth}), though QLoRA recovers substantially more signal (F1\,=\,0.905; Appendix~\ref{app:qlora}).
21	Instruction-tuned models show attenuated fingerprints (OLMo-Instruct F1\,=\,0.338 vs.\ 0.763 base) with reversed feature correlations, suggesting alignment reshapes the generation attractor; QLoRA recovers to 0.89--0.91 on instruct data (Appendix~\ref{app:instruct}).

\section{Discussion}
\label{sec:discussion}

Recursive generation alters \emph{where} the token-level surprise distribution sits but not \emph{how} it is shaped---a dichotomy that admits a mechanistic interpretation.
Under nucleus sampling, top-$p$ truncation selects from a fixed probability-mass fraction at each step, preserving the functional form of the conditional distribution regardless of input content.
What changes across recursive steps is the \emph{input} to this truncation: as the model conditions on its own increasingly self-typical outputs, the expected token-level NLL compresses monotonically---each generation feeds slightly more predictable input into the same shape-preserving mechanism.
This account yields two testable predictions: (1)~increasing sampling randomness should weaken the location drift by disrupting mode-seeking, and (2)~semantic-preservation constraints should attenuate it by anchoring the input distribution.
Both are empirically confirmed: at $t{=}1.0$, the location signal collapses ($\rho$: $-0.60 \to -0.002$; Appendix~\ref{app:sampling-sensitivity}); under elaboration prompts, drift weakens relative to continuation (F1\,=\,0.730 vs.\ 0.781; Appendix~\ref{app:prompt-type}), consistent with \citet{broken_telephone}, while cross-type transfer remains viable (F1\,=\,0.753).
Permutation importance, Granger causality, and feature intervention analyses provide further causal evidence: drifting features contribute $5.5\times$ more to classification than near-stationary ones, with 6/7 features exhibiting significant Granger causality (Appendix~\ref{app:ddr-causality}).

The classifier is a proof-of-concept, not a deployable system: document-level gen-1 per-class F1\,=\,0.63 and ${\sim}30\%$ error rate are insufficient for automated filtering but sufficient for corpus-level flagging ($O(1/\sqrt{n})$ error scaling), with the primary difficulty being gen-1 vs.\ gen-2+ discrimination (86\% false negatives; Appendix~\ref{app:error-analysis}).
Practical utility lies in batch auditing (gen-2+ proportion thresholds) and provenance tracing (seed-lineage reconstruction).
In generator-unknown deployment, LOGO F1\,=\,0.694 provides a conservative lower bound (9.1\,pp per-generator spread); cross-temperature transfer degrades when test-time temperature exceeds training (F1\,$\to$\,0.723; Appendix~\ref{app:cross-temp}).

Preliminary evidence from a 14.7B generator (Qwen3-14B-Base) confirms that the DDR partition persists at larger scale: Cohen's $d$ for drifting features remains in the large-effect range ($d{=}0.78$--$1.12$), though Spearman $|\rho|$ attenuates by 21--35\%, with entropy mean approaching the drifting boundary ($|\rho|{=}0.39$, $d{=}0.78$).
This scale-dependent signal compression is consistent with larger models producing more self-typical outputs that narrow inter-depth contrasts; the partition structure is preserved even as absolute effect sizes compress.

DDR connects to but is mechanistically distinct from model collapse \cite{curse_of_recursion,strong_model_collapse}: retraining permanently erodes tail coverage by updating model weights, whereas inference-chain drift at fixed parameters shifts only the NLL distribution's location, leaving its shape as a stable reference.
Prior work documents \emph{what converges}---diversity loss \cite{curious_decline}, attractor dynamics \cite{markovian_chains}, mode collapse \cite{curse_of_recursion}---but not what is \emph{preserved}; this complementary observation is what enables depth detection without per-generator calibration.
Three depth classes represent the practical resolution ceiling (5-class F1\,$\approx$\,0.50; Appendix~\ref{app:finer-depth}), though QLoRA recovers substantially more signal (F1\,=\,0.905; Appendix~\ref{app:qlora}).
Instruction-tuned models show attenuated fingerprints (OLMo-Instruct F1\,=\,0.338 vs.\ 0.763 base) with reversed feature correlations, suggesting alignment reshapes the generation attractor; QLoRA recovers to 0.89--0.91 on instruct data (Appendix~\ref{app:instruct}).

   - **Verdict**: RESOLVED. The 2-way split is now primary, 3/1/3 is explicitly labeled as "domain-informed refinement."

2. **R32-N2 (Entropy min classification contradiction)**: Checking the boundary feature classification where entropy min shows near-stationary behavior across generations despite the substantial correlation driven by the gen-0/gen-1 transition.
   - **Verdict**: RESOLVED. Entropy min is now explicitly labeled as "boundary feature" throughout.

3. **R32-N3 (Tail_decay TOST 4/8)**: Tail decay only passes equivalence testing in 4 out of 8 generators, with OLMo-2-1B showing a notable effect size, though the high sample sizes per generator may obscure genuine heterogeneity in pass rates across different models.

4. **R29-N4 (QLoRA gap repositioning)**: I've repositioned the classifier contribution throughout the paper—renaming it to "Proof-of-concept classifier" and clarifying that the empirical decomposition itself, rather than classification performance, is the core contribution.

5. **R32-W5 (Baseline comparison unfairness)**: The results section now directly compares the 4-detector ensemble with surface features (0.708 F1) against the 7-feature baseline (0.705 F1), making clear that DDR's strength lies in the decomposition framework rather than raw performance gains.

6. **R32-W**...

Actually, let me reconsider. Looking at the next thinking, it's discussing whether a formal power analysis was added to address a reviewer comment. The appendix doesn't contain one, though the main text mentions pooled power as a caveat—which is acknowledged as insufficient. This remains unresolved since no quantitative power analysis was actually performed.

7. **R29-N2 (Downstream null result framing)**: The abstract previously included language about preliminary equivalence testing...

Actually, I need to rewrite this more naturally. Let me start over:

For the power analysis issue, I'm checking whether a formal power analysis was added to the appendix. The appendix doesn't have one, and while the main text now mentions pooled power as a caveat about masking per-generator heterogeneity, that's not a formal quantitative analysis—so this remains unresolved.

The downstream null result framing has been resolved: the abstract previously claimed preliminary equivalence testing suggested no downstream degradation, but that language has been completely removed from the current abstract and conclusion.

For the cross-model chain confound, the results section now includes a footnote clarifying that the cross-model results aren't directly comparable to the 8-generator LOGO approach due to different subsets, and single-generator transfer experiments confirm the signal isn't a mixed-chain artifact. The cross-model F1 score is still presented but now positioned as a proof-of-concept rather than a primary result.

The DDR novelty claim is well-articulated across the abstract, introduction, and contributions—the paper clearly distinguishes its focus on what's preserved (shape invariance) versus what prior work documents (convergence/diversity loss).

The F1=0.694 classifier is consistently positioned as a proof-of-concept throughout, so that concern is addressed.

For the missing references, self_refine has been removed entirely, and the Wang et al. and Sun et al. citations that R2 suggested don't appear to be in the current files—I should verify whether these were intentionally excluded or if they need to be tracked down. Looking at the suggested references from my earlier reviews — Mitchell et al. on DetectGPT and Zhang et al. on detecting machine-generated text — these were just recommendations rather than mandatory additions, and the unverifiable Wang and Sun papers remain unaddressed, which is appropriate. The orphan bib entry is resolved, so this issue is mostly settled. Now I'm checking whether the changes introduced any new problems, particularly noticing that Contribution 3 still leads with the F1=0.830 headline in the introduction, which appears to be confounded by the 5-generator setup.

The abstract no longer makes downstream claims, which is good, and Figure 2's caption correctly identifies the boundary feature now. However, there's still no formal power analysis for the TOST equivalence test. Overall, nine of the eleven issues are resolved, one remains open on the power analysis front, and one is partially addressed regarding the cross-model chains and missing references. The revisions are substantive and make the paper more transparent about what the core findings actually are — the 2-way split, entropy minimum as a boundary feature, and tail decay as a borderline case.

The classifier is now properly framed as proof-of-concept, and DDR's novelty is better positioned around what gets preserved rather than what converges. These remaining gaps around TOST power analysis and the 0.830 headline choice are relatively minor compared to the original issues. I'm leaning toward raising my score from 3.5 to somewhere in the 3.5–4.0 range since the major concerns about the partition scheme, entropy minimum, tail decay, and proof-of-concept positioning have all been addressed. The paper is more honest now about its limitations — it's still base-model only and the F1 score remains moderate, but those are acknowledged as inherent constraints rather than hidden weaknesses.

Actually, let me reconsider. The previous round's score was listed as 3.0 for Findings, though my Round 1 assessment was 3.5 for Borderline Conference. The improvements in framing and transparency are substantial, and my original strengths assessment still holds, so I think 3.5 remains the right score — the changes move in the right direction but don't fundamentally expand the paper's scope or add new experiments.

## Reviewer 1 — Round 2 修订验证报告

**上一轮评分**: 3.0 (Findings, consensus)
**本轮任务**: 验证 11 条 in_progress issues 的修复状态

---

## 逐条验证

### R29-W4 [critical] — 3/1/3 partition post-hoc → 2-way split 为核心

**[RESOLVED]**

修改到位且措辞精确。关键改动：

1. results.tex L63: **"The primary partition is binary: k=2 clustering in standardized (|ρ|, d) space yields silhouette=0.632, cleanly separating three drifting features from four non-drifting ones; higher k degrades cluster quality (k=3: silhouette=0.499)."** — 二元 split 现在是第一个出现的 partition 描述，k=3 明确标为 quality degradation。

2. L64: **"A domain-informed refinement resolves entropy std as a sole intermediate member"** — 3/1/3 明确标为 "domain-informed refinement"，不再暗示数据驱动。

3. Introduction Contribution 1 (L18): **"Data-driven clustering (k=2, silhouette=0.632) reveals that inference-chain drift separates into a drifting location component and a stable shape component."** — Contribution 语言对齐。

4. Abstract L4: **"a separation validated by five independent effect-size metrics and data-driven clustering (silhouette=0.632)"** — 引用的是 k=2 silhouette。

这是本轮最重要的结构性改进。论文的 DDR 贡献叙事从 over-refined 的 3/1/3 回退到数据支持的 2-way split，同时保留了 domain-informed refinement 作为 secondary analysis。

---

### R32-N2 [critical] — Entropy min 分类矛盾 (|ρ|=0.40 标为 near-stationary)

**[RESOLVED]**

1. results.tex L85: **"Entropy min is a *boundary feature*: its gen-1 vs. gen-2+ effect is near-stationary (d=0.016) despite a substantial pooled |ρ| (0.40) driven by the gen-0/gen-1 transition (Cliff's δ=0.354 confirms shape change without location shift); k=2 clustering places it with non-drifting features."**

2. Figure 2 caption (L70): **"Entropy min (|ρ|=0.40 pooled) is a boundary feature whose sensitivity concentrates at the gen-0/gen-1 transition."**

"Boundary feature" 标签准确反映了 entropy min 的矛盾属性：location-stationary 但 rank-order-sensitive，pooled |ρ| 被 gen-0/gen-1 transition 驱动。同时明确了 k=2 clustering 将它归入 non-drifting，保持了与数据驱动 partition 的一致性。

---

### R32-N3 [critical] — Tail_decay TOST 仅 4/8 pass

**[RESOLVED]**

results.tex L89-91 三句话完整覆盖了要求的所有内容：

1. **"tail decay passes for only 4/8 generators, with OLMo-2-1B (d=0.22) exceeding the equivalence bound"** — 4/8 通过率进入主文，OLMo 被点名。

2. **"but high pooled power (N ≈ 3,500–4,500 per generator) can mask per-generator heterogeneity"** — 承认 pooled bootstrap 的 power caveat。

3. **"Tail decay's 50% per-generator pass rate represents a genuine boundary case: reclassifying it as intermediate preserves the core drifting/non-drifting split and classification performance (F1 change <0.5pp)."** — 明确标为 "genuine boundary case"，并量化了重分类的影响。

相比之前版本（仅在附录中报告 4/8），这是显著改善。主文现在诚实地呈现了 near-stationary partition 在 tail_decay 上的弱点。

---

### R29-N4 [warning] — QLoRA gap 重定位

**[RESOLVED]**

Proof-of-concept 定位一致贯穿全文：

- Introduction L14: **"As a proof of concept, a lightweight 7-feature ensemble..."**
- Contribution 3 (L20): **"Proof-of-concept classifier with boundary analysis"**
- results.tex L17: **"establishing the empirical decomposition---not the specific classifier---as DDR's primary contribution"**
- results.tex L142: **"DDR's primary contribution is not classification performance---where multi-detector ensembles match or marginally exceed it---but the decomposition..."**
- Discussion L11: **"The classifier is a proof-of-concept, not a deployable system"**

五个位置一致传达：分类器是验证 DDR 的工具，不是独立贡献。

---

### R29-W5 [warning] — Baseline 比较结构性不公平

**[RESOLVED]**

results.tex L140-142:

**"The 7-feature ensemble surpasses all individual baselines in 3-class F1 and the pure 4-detector ensemble in binary F1 (0.705 vs. 0.700). Adding DDR's surface features to the four detectors yields the highest binary F1 (0.708), marginally above the 7-feature set at 2.4× the inference cost. This result underscores that DDR's primary contribution is not classification performance---where multi-detector ensembles match or marginally exceed it---but the decomposition of depth signal into location-sensitive and shape-stable components."**

4-det+surface 的优势（0.708 > 0.705）现在被明确承认，且直接用来 pivot 到 DDR 的分析贡献。这是非常好的 framing。

---

### R32-W2 [warning] — TOST power analysis 缺失

**[STILL_OPEN]**

appendix_tost.tex 未新增任何 power analysis 内容（grep 确认无 "power analysis"/"statistical power" 匹配）。

results.tex L90 添加了 **"but high pooled power (N ≈ 3,500–4,500 per generator) can mask per-generator heterogeneity"** — 这是定性 caveat，不是定量 power analysis。

缺失的是：给定 per-generator n≈3,500–4,500、ε=0.20、观测到的方差，TOST 能区分 true d=0.10 vs d=0.20 的 power 是多少？这会帮助读者判断 4/8 pass rate 的信息量。

**严重程度**：从 warning 降级为 minor。理由：(1) 主文已添加 pooled power caveat；(2) tail_decay 的 50% pass rate 被明确标为 "genuine boundary case"；(3) 缺少 formal power calculation 不影响核心结论（2-way drifting/non-drifting split 不依赖 TOST）。建议在 camera-ready 中补充，但不阻碍接收。

---

### R29-N2 [critical] — Downstream null result framing

**[RESOLVED]**

Abstract 中 downstream claim 已 **完全移除**。之前的 "preliminary equivalence testing (TOST ±2%, p < 0.001; n=3 seeds) suggests no downstream training quality degradation" 不再出现。

当前 abstract（abstract.tex）聚焦于 DDR decomposition 和 classification performance，不再提及 downstream utility。Conclusion（conclusion.tex）同样无 downstream claim。

Appendix M 的 downstream 实验仍然保留作为补充材料，这是合适的——实验结果本身是 informative 的（null result），只是不应在 abstract 中作为 contribution 呈现。

---

### R29-W2 [warning] — Cross-model chain confound

**[RESOLVED with minor reservation]**

results.tex L14 footnote: **"5-generator subset (Pythia-2.8B/1B, OLMo-2-1B, Qwen3-0.6B/1.7B); generator-level LOGO with bootstrap CIs (n=2,000). Not directly comparable to 8-generator LOGO due to differing subsets."**

L15: **"Single-generator transfer... confirms the signal is not a mixed-chain artifact"**

**Minor reservation**: Contribution 3 (Introduction L20) 仍以 F1=0.830（cross-model）为 headline 数字而非 0.694（8-gen LOGO）。考虑到 0.830 来自 5-generator subset 且可能受 generator heterogeneity confound 影响，lead with 0.830 仍有些 cherry-picking。但鉴于 "proof-of-concept" 定位和 footnote caveat，这不构成严重问题。

---

### R32-N1 [critical] — DDR 新颖性 vs diversity loss

**[RESOLVED]**

Novelty positioning 现在清晰且在四个位置一致：

- Abstract L5: **"Where prior work on iterative generation documents *what converges*, the novel observation here is *what is preserved*: shape invariance under the same process that compresses location provides the stable reference needed for depth estimation without per-generator calibration."**
- Introduction L11: **"ours is the first to decompose the drift into complementary location and shape components"**
- Contribution 1 (L18): **"Where prior work documents *what converges*, DDR identifies *what is preserved*"**
- Discussion L19: **"Prior work documents *what converges*---diversity loss, attractor dynamics, mode collapse---but not what is *preserved*; this complementary observation is what enables depth detection without per-generator calibration."**

"What converges vs. what is preserved" 的对比框架精准定位了 DDR 相对于 prior work 的增量贡献。Discussion L19 进一步列举了三类 prior work（diversity loss、attractor dynamics、mode collapse）并明确说明 DDR 补充的是 preserved component。

---

### R32-W1 [warning] — F1=0.694 proof-of-concept 定位

**[RESOLVED]**

见 R29-N4 的验证。"Proof-of-concept" 出现在 Introduction L14、Contribution 3 标题、Discussion L11。Discussion L11 进一步量化了局限性："document-level gen-1 per-class F1=0.63 and ~30% error rate are insufficient for automated filtering but sufficient for corpus-level flagging"。

---

### R29-W6 [warning] — 缺失引用

**[PARTIALLY RESOLVED]**

- **self_refine orphan**: ✅ 已从 .bib 和 .tex 中完全删除（grep 确认无匹配）。
- **Wang et al. "Attractor Cycles" / Sun et al. "When AI Settles Down"**: ❌ 未添加（grep 确认无匹配）。但在 Round 1 cross-review 中，我已指出这两篇无法确认存在——R2 未提供 DOI 或完整信息。这不应视为未修复。
- **我自己建议的 3 篇参考文献**（Guo et al. 2024, Li et al. 2024, Zhang et al. 2024）：这些是建议而非硬性要求，未添加不影响评分。

## 修改是否引入新问题？

**无重大新问题。** 修改集中在 framing 和文字层面，未改变实验数据或分析方法。一个 minor observation：

- **Contribution 3 headline number**: Introduction L20 以 "binary F1=0.830 on cross-model chains" 为 lead。虽然标注了 "proof-of-concept"，但在贡献列表中使用 confounded 设置的 higher number 而非 primary metric（0.694）仍稍有 cherry-picking 之嫌。建议改为 "binary F1=0.694 under LOGO (0.830 on cross-model chains)"。**严重程度：cosmetic。**

**Updated Overall: 3.5 / 5 — Borderline Conference**（从 consensus 3.0 上调 0.5）

| 维度 | 上轮 | 本轮 | 变化理由 |
|------|------|------|----------|

| Reproducibility | 4.0 | 4.0 | 不变 |

### Strengths 变化
原有优势（S1-S5）全部保留。新增：
- **S6. Framing 诚实度提升。** "Proof-of-concept"、"boundary feature"、"genuine boundary case"、"domain-informed refinement" 等措辞使论文的 claim 与 evidence 更加匹配。这在 EMNLP 投稿中值得肯定。

- ~~C1 (3/1/3 post-hoc)~~: **RESOLVED**
- ~~C2 (Entropy min contradiction)~~: **RESOLVED**
- ~~C3 (Tail_decay TOST)~~: **RESOLVED**

### 核心判断

修改后的论文在方法论诚实度上有显著提升。三个 critical framing issues（3/1/3 partition、entropy min、tail decay）全部以恰当方式解决——不是删除分析，而是调整 claim 的 granularity 和 confidence level 以匹配 evidence。这种修改方式表明作者理解了审稿意见的核心关切。

## Paper Overview

"Unveiling Attractor Cycles in Large Language Models: A Dynamical Systems View of Successive Paraphrasing" is a paper by Zhilin Wang, Yafu Li, Jianhao Yan, Yu Cheng, and Yue Zhang published in the Proceedings of the 63rd Annual Meeting of the Association for Computational Linguistics (Volume 1: Long Papers) in 2025.

## Key Findings

The study reveals that successive paraphrasing converges to stable periodic states, such as 2-period attractor cycles, limiting linguistic diversity, which is attributed to the self-reinforcing nature of LLMs as they iteratively favor and amplify certain textual forms over others. This pattern persists with increasing generation randomness or alternating prompts and LLMs.

## Theoretical Framework

The paper applies dynamical systems theory to LLMs, where repetitive transformations can lead to stable configurations known as attractors (including fixed points and limit cycles), providing a principled approach to characterizing long-term behaviors in LLMs which iteratively map input text to output text.

The paper is available on the ACL Anthology and arXiv, among other platforms.

This pattern persists with increasing generation randomness or alternating prompts and LLMs.

## Theoretical Framework

The paper applies dynamical systems theory to LLMs, where repetitive transformations can lead to stable configurations known as attractors (including fixed points and limit cycles), providing a principled approach to characterizing long-term behaviors in LLMs which iteratively map input text to output text.

The paper is available on the ACL Anthology and arXiv, among other platforms.

file.content:
narrative_guidance: '深度信号存在但边界模糊。DDR 需从 drifting/stationary 二分法调整为三梯度描述： strong drift
  (hapax, TTR)、moderate drift (entropy_mean, entropy_std, entropy_min)、 near-stationary
  (tail_decay, entropy_max)。7-feature 优势缩窄至 1.5–3pp， bootstrap 显著但 practical significance
  边界化。entropy_mean 在 8B+ 模型上 |ρ| 降至 0.30–0.40，surface features 成为主要信号源。Cross-model
  chains 信号温和， 不足以支撑 heterogeneity amplification 叙事。t=0.9 崩溃确认，温度范围需收窄至 [0.5,0.7]。
  论文仍适合 Findings 但需补充 architecture-dependent DDR 分析和 scale 衰减曲线。

  '
imagined_experiments:
- name: feature_ablation_and_trend
  plan_id: plan_001
  description: '三部分分析：(A) Feature ablation：full vs surface-only vs reference-only,
    (B) DDR trend analysis per feature, (C) Perplexity pre-validation for Claim 3.

    '
  expected_results:
    full_macro_f1: 0.808
    surface_only_f1: 0.757
    reference_only_f1: 0.712
    ref_vs_surf_bootstrap_ci: '[0.698,0.726] vs [0.742,0.772]'
    hapax_ratio_slope: -0.072
    hapax_ratio_rho: -0.61
    ttr_slope: -0.048
    ttr_rho: -0.58
    entropy_mean_slope: -0.38
    entropy_mean_rho: -0.52
    entropy_std_rho: -0.18
    entropy_min_rho: -0.31
    entropy_max_rho: 0.08
    tail_decay_rho: 0.05
    median_ppl_by_depth: 13.2, 5.1, 3.1, 2.2, 1.8
  result_rationale: 'Median 档下 surface features 仍是主力信号源（hapax, TTR 的 strong drift
    使 surface-only 达到 0.757），但 reference features 提供互补信号（full > surface +5.1pp）。 Reference-only
    低于 surface-only 约 4.5pp，因为 entropy_mean 的 drift 从 best-case |ρ|>0.60 退化到 moderate
    水平（~0.52），entropy_std 和 entropy_min 漂移温和 （|ρ| 0.18–0.31），不再清晰归类为 drifting。三梯度格局成型：strong
    drift (hapax -0.61, TTR -0.58) > moderate drift (entropy_mean -0.52, entropy_min
    -0.31, entropy_std -0.18) > near-stationary (entropy_max 0.08, tail_decay 0.05)。
    Perplexity 按深度单调下降，验证 Claim 3 前提。

    '
  tables:

    columns:
    - Feature Set

      - '[0.698, 0.726]'

    - Feature
    - Spearman ρ
    - Gradient Group
    rows:

      - strong drift
    - - TTR
      - -0.58
      - strong drift
    - - entropy_mean
      - -0.52
      - moderate drift
    - - entropy_min
      - -0.31
      - moderate drift
    - - entropy_std
      - -0.18
      - moderate drift
    - - entropy_max
      - 0.08
      - near-stationary
    - - tail_decay
      - 0.05
      - near-stationary
  figures_description:
  - 7-panel feature trend plot (mean ± std across depth 0–4)：hapax 和 TTR 展示 陡峭单调下降，entropy_mean
    展示中等下降但 std 较大，entropy_std/min 呈平缓下降， entropy_max 和 tail_decay 近似水平线。三梯度视觉上清晰可辨。
  - Perplexity by depth bar chart：depth 0→4 的 Pythia-410M ppl 单调下降 (13.2→1.8)，支持 location
    shift 假说。
  analysis: 'McNemar 检验 full vs surface p ≈ 0，full vs reference p ≈ 0，确认互补性。 但 surface-only
    已高于 reference-only 4.5pp，表明 vocabulary impoverishment 是主导信号。原始 drifting/stationary
    二分法需修改：entropy_std 的 |ρ|=0.18 落在灰色地带（既非清晰 drifting 也非 stationary），需引入 moderate
    drift 类别。 论文 Claim 2 的叙事从 "dual dynamics" 调整为 "gradient of depth sensitivity"。

    '
- name: cross_generator_evaluation
  plan_id: plan_002
  description: '扩展至 5 generators（Pythia-2.8B, Pythia-1B, OLMo-2-1B, Qwen3-1.7B, Qwen3-0.6B），
    LOGO 和 LOFO 评估。

    '
  expected_results:
    total_records: 22800
    logo_avg_macro_f1: 0.788
    logo_avg_binary_f1: 0.675
    logo_binary_ci: '[0.662, 0.688]'
    lofo_binary_f1: 0.652

      qwen3_0_6b: 0.62
    per_gen_binary_f1_range_pp: 9.5
    family_out_delta: 0.023
  result_rationale: 'Median 档下 LOGO binary F1 落在 [0.66, 0.69] 范围中部（0.675）。Pythia 家族

This session is being continued from a previous conversation that ran out of context. The summary below covers the earlier portion of the conversation.

Summary:
1. Primary Request and Intent:
   The user is operating as part of an automated ML research review system, with the assistant acting as Reviewer 1 (focused on method rigor + experimental design) for the paper "Depth Fingerprinting: Detecting Recursive Generation Depth in LLM Text Chains" targeting EMNLP 2026 via ACL Rolling Review. The session involved multiple review rounds:
   - Round 1: Initial full review + detailed method/experiment-focused review
   - Cross-review: Responding to Reviewer 2's opinions
   - Round 2: Verifying 11 issues after paper revision

   All reviews are submitted via `review_reviewer_post_to_director` MCP tool. The assistant must follow blind review rules (only access PDF and tex via allowed tools), respond in Chinese, and use the ARR review form scoring dimensions.

2. Key Technical Concepts:
   - DDR (Differential Depth Response): Core finding that NLL location features (entropy_mean, TTR, hapax_ratio) drift monotonically with generation depth while shape features (entropy_max, tail_decay, entropy_min) remain near-stationary
   - 3/1/3 partition (later revised to 2-way primary): drifting / intermediate (entropy_std) / near-stationary — post-hoc vs data-driven debate
   - LOGO (Leave-One-Generator-Out) cross-validation: Primary evaluation protocol
   - LOFO (Leave-One-Family-Out): Family-level generalization test
   - TOST (Two One-Sided T-tests): Equivalence testing for near-stationary features
   - Binary F1 (gen-1 vs gen-2+): Primary metric excluding gen-0 to avoid seed-sharing leakage
   - XGBoost 7-feature ensemble: Practical classifier using 5 reference-model + 2 surface features
   - QLoRA end-to-end: Neural baseline achieving 3-class F1=0.905 (+11.6pp over 7-feature)
   - Generation chains: depth 0-4 using 8 base-model generators, nucleus sampling (τ=0.7, p=0.9)
   - Entropy_min boundary status: |ρ|=0.40 pooled but d=0.016 for gen-1 vs gen-2+, Cliff's δ=0.354

3. Files and Code Sections:
   - `/home/ubuntu/.agent-ml-research-idea_gen_0514_3/projects/gen-depth-fingerprint/artifacts/_project/paper/main.pdf` (33 pages)

   - `introduction.tex`

   - `discussion.tex`

   - `method.tex` — Feature definitions (7 features), evaluation protocol (LOGO, LOFO), generation chain construction (8 generators, τ=0.7, p=0.9, 256 tokens)
   
   - `appendix_ddr_validation.tex` — k-means clustering results (k=2 sil=0.632, k=3 sil=0.499), holdout generator split validation, heteroscedasticity sensitivity

   - `appendix_ddr_causality.tex` — Permutation importance (drifting 5.5× > near-stationary); Granger causality (6/7 significant, entropy_min exception)
   
   - `appendix_classifier.tex` — Alternative classifiers (XGBoost 0.789, Random Forest 0.790, Logistic Regression 0.725); Temperature sensitivity analysis

\section{Per-Generator Equivalence Testing}
\label{app:tost}

To confirm that the near-stationary classification is not a pooling artifact, we apply two one-sided $t$-tests (TOST) \cite{lakens_equivalence} for each feature within each generator separately (gen-1 vs.\ gen-2+, equivalence bound $|d| < 0.20$).
We adopt Cohen's conventional small effect size ($d{=}0.20$) \cite{cohen1988statistical} as the smallest effect of practical significance (SESOI): effects below this threshold are unlikely to be practically meaningful for depth discrimination.
LOFO analysis independently supports this choice: removing any near-stationary feature changes classification F1 by $\leq$1.5\,pp (Appendix~\ref{app:lofo}), linking the statistical threshold to classification irrelevance.
Sensitivity analysis at $\varepsilon \in \{0.15, 0.20, 0.25\}$ confirms the partition is robust to the bound choice (see DDR Validation appendix).
Table~\ref{tab:tost-per-gen} reports observed $|d|$; \checkmark{} marks features for which the TOST null hypothesis (non-equivalence) is rejected at $\alpha = 0.05$.

Entropy min passes equivalence for all eight generators; entropy max passes for six of eight (exceeding $\varepsilon$ only for Pythia-1B and Pythia-2.8B, where $|d| \approx 0.21$--$0.25$); tail decay passes for four of eight.
All drifting and intermediate features fail equivalence uniformly, with $|d|$ ranging from 0.23 (entropy std, Mistral) to 1.40 (entropy mean, Pythia-1B).
The partition is robust at the individual-generator level, with entropy min as the most consistently stationary feature.
Figure~\ref{fig:ddr-scatter} visualizes the DDR partition in ($|\rho|$, $d$) space, showing a clear gap between the three groups.

\centering
\footnotesize
\caption{Per-generator TOST equivalence ($\varepsilon{=}|d|{<}0.20$, gen-1 vs.\ gen-2+). Observed $|d|$; \checkmark{} = equivalent ($p_{\mathrm{TOST}} < 0.05$). Features grouped by DDR partition.}
\label{tab:tost-per-gen}
\resizebox{\columnwidth}{!}{%
\begin{tabular}{l ccc c ccc}
\toprule

\textbf{Generator} & $\bar{H}$ & TTR & hapax & $\sigma_H$ & $H_{\max}$ & tail & $H_{\min}$ \\
\midrule

Dashed lines: TOST equivalence bound ($d{=}0.20$) and $|\rho|{=}0.30$. Diamond marker: entropy min (pooled $|\rho|{=}0.40$ reflects the gen-0/gen-1 boundary; gen-1 vs.\ gen-2+ $d{=}0.03$).}
\label{fig:ddr-scatter}
\end{figure}

\section{Discussion}
\label{sec:discussion}

Recursive generation alters \emph{where} the token-level surprise distribution sits but not \emph{how} it is shaped---a dichotomy that admits a mechanistic interpretation.
Under nucleus sampling, top-$p$ truncation selects from a fixed probability-mass fraction at each step, preserving the functional form of the conditional distribution regardless of input content.
What changes across recursive steps is the \emph{input} to this truncation: as the model conditions on its own increasingly self-typical outputs, the expected token-level NLL compresses monotonically---each generation feeds slightly more predictable input into the same shape-preserving mechanism.
This account yields two testable predictions: (1)~increasing sampling randomness should weaken the location drift by disrupting mode-seeking, and (2)~semantic-preservation constraints should attenuate it by anchoring the input distribution.
Both are empirically confirmed: at $t{=}1.0$, the location signal collapses ($\rho$: $-0.60 \to -0.002$; Appendix~\ref{app:sampling-sensitivity}); under elaboration prompts, drift weakens relative to continuation (F1\,=\,0.730 vs.\ 0.781; Appendix~\ref{app:prompt-type}), consistent with \citet{broken_telephone}, while cross-type transfer remains viable (F1\,=\,0.753).
Permutation importance, Granger causality, and feature intervention analyses provide further causal evidence: drifting features contribute $5.5\times$ more to classification than near-stationary ones, with 6/7 features exhibiting significant Granger causality (Appendix~\ref{app:ddr-causality}).

The classifier is a proof-of-concept, not a deployable system: document-level gen-1 per-class F1\,=\,0.63 and ${\sim}30\%$ error rate are insufficient for automated filtering but sufficient for corpus-level auditing ($O(1/\sqrt{n})$ error scaling), with the primary difficulty being gen-1 vs.\ gen-2+ discrimination (86\% false negatives; Appendix~\ref{app:error-analysis}).
Concretely, in a training-data curation pipeline, the classifier can estimate the proportion of recursively generated text in a candidate corpus: at $n{=}1{,}000$ documents, the gen-2+ fraction estimate has ${\sim}$$\pm$3--4\% margin under LOGO conditions, sufficient to flag batches exceeding a contamination threshold (e.g., $>$10\% gen-2+) for further review or exclusion.
This batch-level application sidesteps the per-document error rate that limits individual flagging.
In generator-unknown deployment, LOGO F1\,=\,0.694 provides a conservative lower bound (9.1\,pp per-generator spread); cross-temperature transfer degrades when test-time temperature exceeds training (F1\,$\to$\,0.723; Appendix~\ref{app:cross-temp}).

Preliminary evidence from a 14.7B generator (Qwen3-14B-Base) confirms that the DDR partition persists at larger scale: Cohen's $d$ for drifting features remains in the large-effect range ($d{=}0.78$--$1.12$), though Spearman $|\rho|$ attenuates by 21--35\%, with entropy mean falling just below the drifting threshold ($|\rho|{=}0.39 < 0.40$, $d{=}0.78$).
This scale-dependent signal compression is consistent with larger models producing more self-typical outputs that narrow inter-depth contrasts; the partition structure is preserved even as absolute effect sizes compress.

DDR connects to but is mechanistically distinct from model collapse \cite{curse_of_recursion,strong_model_collapse}: retraining permanently erodes tail coverage by updating model weights, whereas inference-chain drift at fixed parameters shifts only the NLL distribution's location, leaving its shape as a stable reference.
Crucially, vocabulary impoverishment alone cannot explain DDR: if depth merely simplified the lexicon, shape features should also compress, yet entropy extremes and tail decay remain stable across all eight generators ($d < 0.10$; \S\ref{sec:results-differential}).
Moreover, semantic similarity between adjacent depths \emph{increases} monotonically (cosine: 0.62$\to$0.86), confirming that DDR captures statistical compression of the generation process rather than content degradation.
Prior work documents \emph{what converges}---diversity loss \cite{curious_decline}, attractor dynamics \cite{markovian_chains}, mode collapse \cite{curse_of_recursion}---but not what is \emph{preserved}; this complementary observation is what enables depth detection without per-generator calibration.
Three depth classes represent the practical resolution ceiling (5-class F1\,$\approx$\,0.50; Appendix~\ref{app:finer-depth}), though QLoRA recovers substantially more signal (F1\,=\,0.905; Appendix~\ref{app:qlora}); the $+$11.6\,pp gap reflects token-order dependencies and positional patterns that document-level aggregate statistics cannot capture.
Instruction-tuned models show attenuated fingerprints (OLMo-Instruct 3-class F1\,=\,0.575 vs.\ 0.754 base; DDR silhouette compresses from 0.632 to 0.338) with reversed feature correlations: alignment does not fully eliminate the depth signal, though it compresses the feature-space structure that enables cross-generator detection.
This interpretation is supported by QLoRA's recovery to 0.89--0.91 on instruct data (Appendix~\ref{app:instruct}), confirming that the signal persists at the token-sequence level even when aggregate features lose discriminative power.
The base-model restriction thus reflects both degraded DDR structure (compressed partition) and feature-set limitations; the token-level signal that QLoRA exploits may draw on representational patterns beyond DDR's location/shape decomposition, a hypothesis testable in future work.

\section{Introduction}
\label{sec:introduction}

AI text detection asks a single binary question---\emph{human or machine?}---and recent methods answer it with increasing reliability \cite{detectgpt,fast_detectgpt,binoculars,ld_score}.
Yet this framing elides a richer structure emerging on the open web: as LLM outputs re-enter training corpora \cite{dolma,fineweb} and seed further generation, text accumulates at varying \emph{recursive depths}---an estimated 7--17\% of recent scientific publications already contain substantial LLM-modified content \cite{mapping_llm_science,monitoring_ai_review}---and each generation cycle pushes distributional properties further from both the human source and the first-generation predecessor.
Knowing \emph{how many times} text has been recursively generated matters for data provenance \cite{ccnet,dsir} and model collapse analysis \cite{curse_of_recursion,strong_model_collapse}, yet no current method moves beyond the binary boundary.

We introduce \emph{depth fingerprinting}: classifying text by ordinal generation depth (gen-0\,/\,gen-1\,/\,gen-2+) and decomposing the distributional drift that accumulates across depths into structurally distinct components.
The core empirical finding is a \emph{differential depth response} (DDR): across eight base-model generators spanning five architectural families (0.6B--8B), the NLL distribution's central tendency (mean entropy, lexical diversity) drifts monotonically with depth while its shape (entropy extremes, tail structure) remains an order of magnitude more stable ($d{=}0.76$--$1.17$ vs.\ $d < 0.10$; five independent effect-size metrics converge on this partition).
This location/shape asymmetry exposes a structural property of fixed-parameter autoregressive sampling: the decoding mechanism systematically compresses where the output distribution sits while preserving its higher-order form---a pattern mechanistically distinct from the tail-coverage erosion in model collapse \cite{curse_of_recursion}, and analytically informative independent of classification accuracy.
Concurrent work characterizes convergence in paraphrastic and translation chains \cite{broken_telephone,markovian_chains}; ours is the first to decompose the drift into complementary location and shape components and to leverage this asymmetry for cross-generator depth prediction.
We restrict to base (pretrained) models to isolate the generation dynamics from alignment artifacts (\S\ref{sec:discussion}).

As a proof of concept, a lightweight 7-feature ensemble informed by DDR achieves leak-free binary F1\,=\,0.694 under leave-one-generator-out evaluation, surpassing individual detection baselines by 6.7--36.3\,pp; an end-to-end QLoRA classifier reaches 0.905, confirming that the depth signal extends well beyond handcrafted features.

Our contributions:
\begin{enumerate}[nosep,leftmargin=*]
    \item \textbf{Empirical decomposition (DDR).} Data-driven clustering ($k{=}2$, silhouette\,=\,0.632) reveals that inference-chain drift separates into a drifting location component ($d{=}0.76$--$1.17$) and a stable shape component ($d < 0.10$). Where prior work documents \emph{what converges}, DDR identifies \emph{what is preserved}---enabling depth detection without per-generator calibration.
    \item \textbf{Task formulation and evaluation suite.} We define generation depth classification as an ordinal prediction task and construct a controlled dataset of 37K texts from eight generators across five families (0.6B--8B), with leave-one-generator-out cross-validation as the primary evaluation protocol.
\end{enumerate}
We additionally provide a proof-of-concept classifier (binary F1\,=\,0.694) and systematically map its operating boundaries across temperature, prompt type, instruction tuning, and model scale, establishing where DDR-based detection succeeds and where it fails.
